entities.description:
Nuvema Town is a location that was introduced in Generation V. The town is home to the player character and their two friends (Cheren and Bianca) in Pokémon Black Version and Pokémon White Version. In both Pokémon Black and White and their sequels, it is home to Professor Juniper's lab as well.

Located in the southeastern end of the Unova region, Nuvema Town is a tiny, rural town that's breezy and surrounded by trees. It also overlooks the sea on the southern side (with metal guard rails to prevent anyone from falling and four supporting pillars dug into the sea), and its motto is "The Start of Something Big!". Directly north of the town is Route 1, a small route filled with vegetation and wild Pokémon.

In terms of housing, the town has three identical blue-roofed brown houses with green hedges on the sides, each one belonging to a specific family—the southeast house belongs to Cheren's family, the southwest one belongs to Bianca's family, and the middle one belongs to the player character's family. Professor Juniper's lab also sits in the town's northwest corner.

In all of its in-game appearances, Nuvema Town only has ten people living within its borders.

entities.description:
Undella Town is a large resort town in eastern Unova. To the east of the town is Undella Bay, where you can access an underwater temple known as the Abyssal Ruins. Undella Town is also home to Unova's famous underwater Marine Tube that serves as a bridge between the town and Humilau City}}.

Cynthia also often visits the town and stays in her friend's (Caitlin) villa where she can be battled in the Spring and Summer.

In this town, you can also sell any items you might find during your exploration in the Abyssal Ruins to a collector residing in the Riches' house in the west, where the two younger 'Rich' children battle you once per day.

There are various Pokémon throughout the area, which can be obtained by fishing or surfing. The encounter level will range from 25 to 70. Also, in summer, a woman in a villa offers to trade her Munchlax for a Cinccino.

entities.description:
Sabrina, also known by her title The Master of Psychic Pokémon, is a character debuting in Pocket Monsters Red and Pocket Monsters Green. She is the Saffron City Gym Leader and, hence the title she bears, is an adept user of -type Pokémon. Sabrina is fought in the Saffron City Gym, where she gives the Marsh Badge to Trainers who defeat her in a Pokémon battle. She possesses psychic abilities and specializes in -type Pokémon.

Sabrina is a slender young woman of medium height. She has long black hair with shorter layers around her face and a fringe and small reddish-purple eyes. She wears a small red and dress black in the middle at the waist with a slit on the sides with yellow cuffs over black tights/leggings, white gloves and red and yellow knee-high boots.

In Pokémon HeartGold Version and Pokémon SoulSilver Version, Sabrina has shorter navy hair, now around shoulder length, wears a tight-fitting spaghetti strap pink crop top that shows off her midriff and shoulders, white slim fit ultra low-rise pants (which reveals her hips and some area above) attached with a black belt with a silver colored hexagonal belt buckle below her hips and pink slip on shoes. She also wears green and black bracelets on her wrists that glow on certain sections.

Sabrina appears in Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! and Pokémon: Let's Go, Eevee! with a similar outfit, but her dress has black sleeves and an X is added, she also wears green boots.

entities.description:
Roark serves as the Gym Leader for Oreburgh City's Gym and is the son of the Canalave City Gym Leader, Byron. Roark specializes in using -type Pokémon and holds the Coal Badge for the trainers who defeat him.

Roark is a young man with red hair, who wears glasses. He wears a mining outfit, consisted of gray short-sleeved jacket and baggy pants with yellow/black outlines, which are tucked into his boots. The boots has red soles underneath them. He has a black tank underneath. Roark also wears white gloves with yellow outlines, and is usually seen with a red mining helmet.

Roark is a fair and reasonable trainer, with equal love and respect for all Pokémon. He has a father-son rivalry with his father, Byron of which he's determined to surpass him. However, with his inexperience, this feud still remains today.

The name Roark comes from "rock" and "ore".

entities.short_description: The is a historical place located in the Johto region in the south-west of Violet City with entrances to the south of Route 36 and west of Route 32. It is a famed place for archaeologists who are researching the ruins…
entities.description:
The is a historical place located in the Johto region in the south-west of Violet City with entrances to the south of Route 36 and west of Route 32. It is a famed place for archaeologists who are researching the ruins to discover the mystery of the mysterious Pokémon called the Unown. The ruins are filled with Unown once any of the four slide puzzles inside have been activated.

In the Ruins of Alph, there are four puzzles that are considered to be the keys to enter the dimension of the Unown in the same room as where there are no puzzles. Those four puzzles contain a historical Pokémon or a Legendary Pokémon. The puzzles that appear in Pokémon Gold, Silver and Crystal are really different than the puzzles that are introduced in the renewal version of Pokémon Gold Version and Pokémon Silver Version; Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver.

{|style="margin:auto; width:310px; padding:2px; border:2px solid #FFD700; background-color:#BFC1C2; color:#000; text-align:center; " cellspacing=1 !Kabuto !Aerodactyl !Ho-Oh !Omanyte

Kabuto is actually the first puzzle that you will encounter in the Ruins of Alph, actually, each of the four puzzles can be the first puzzle that you can solve. The puzzle of Kabuto is also the easiest puzzle that you can solve. To get access to the first puzzle, you must enter the cave that is very close to the entrance of the Ruins of Alph which is just above the Research Center if you come from another entrance. Once entered, on the right side you will read the description of the puzzle containing to be: "A Pokémon that hid on the sea floor. Eyes on its back scanned the area".

entities.description:
The Burned Tower is a location introduced in Generation II.

The Burned Tower is a location in Ecruteak City, in the Johto region. It stands beside the Bell Tower. In , Burned Tower resembles the Bell Tower, but with fewer floors. In and , the roof is burnt down to better reflect the destruction that had occurred to it. The Burned Tower is one of the locations where the rival is fought, and defeating him in is required for the Ecruteak City Gym to become accessible.

The Burned Tower is named for the fact that it had been burned down when struck by a lightning bolt. Before the tower burned down, it was titled the Brass Tower. Lugia used to reside in the Burned Tower before moving to the Whirl Islands. Raikou, Entei, and Suicune—the three Legendary Beasts—were unable to escape the tower when it burned down, but Ho-Oh later came along to revive them.

In , a level 40 Suicune appears here as their next destination if the player does not catch it on Route 25. Suicune begins to appear only after the player enters the Hall of Fame, and if it not caught at the Burned Tower, Suicune does not appear again unless the player re-enters the Hall of Fame.

entities.description:
Accumula Town is a small town in Unova renowned for its hills and great views, nestled between Route 1 and Route 2 in south-eastern Unova. It's the second town you'll visit on your adventure in Black and White, and the very first time you'll encounter N, Ghetsis, and Team Plasma.

Professor Juniper will explain how to heal your Pokémon and purchase items from the redesigned Pokémon Center and mentions her friend, Fennel. Ghetsis of Team Plasma, surrounded by townspeople, speaks about liberating Pokémon, and one boy in the crowd seems to be particularly interested in the speech. Afterward, the mysterious boy introduces himself as N and challenges you to a battle.

entities.description:
Clay is the Gym Leader at Driftveil City's Gym. His gym is the fifth gym to be challenged by the trainer. He specializes in using -type Pokémon. He will award the player character the Quake Badge if defeated. A resident of Nimbasa City, Clay's outfit resembles that of a Texan businessman and he has a Texan accent.

Clay is a large man with curly dark brown hair and dark eyes. Clay wears a large cowboy hat, with a yellow stripe and a teal gem on the front. Clay also wears a sleeveless jacket, with small ribbons on his chest, as well as a hazel shirt underneath. He also wears teal pants, with a belt with a yellow buckle, underneath his large brown ones, as well as a pair of dark shoes. Clay is usually seen with his large suitcase and has a watch on his left arm. Clay is of Sinnohan descent, making him equivalent to a Japanese-American.

Although Clay is shown to be impatient and hotheaded, he is good of heart and cares greatly for his hometown, Driftveil City, and for the Unova region as a whole. He is willing to put aside his role of Gym Leader to protect Driftveil from antagonistic people, specifically Team Plasma. Clay pioneered Driftveil's redevelopment between Black & White and Black & White 2 and founded the Pokémon World Tournament to increase the city's popularity.

The name Clay comes from "clay", a type of sticky, fine-grained soil, often used to make pottery, bricks, and ceramics.

entities.description:
Juan is the Gym Leader at Sootopolis City's Gym in the Hoenn region, who specializes in -type Pokémon, where he replaced the former Gym Leader, Wallace, in Emerald. Like Wallace he will award the player character the Rain Badge if he is defeated. He is very popular with the citizens of Sootopolis City.

Juan is a tail man with dark eyes, a small, trimmed moustache and black hair with a white streak, and two white locks standing out in the front and one on his right side of the head. Juan wears a skin tight black suit, a regal blue mantle, a white scarf with a blue gem etched into it. He also wears purple cargo shorts and a pair of white penny loafers.

Juan is described as a sophisticated and elegant but also an attractively dashing gentleman, which has enamored a lot of ladies. He emphasizes greatly on the grace and poise in battling, and hopes that fellow Trainers can battle in a graceful manner as well.

The name Juan comes from "water," as the "Jua" in "Juan" and the "wa" in "water" are pronounced the same. It is also likely that his name is a reference to legendary womanizer Don Juan, as he fits the archetype of the dashing romantic. His many female fans support this theory.

entities.description:
Veilstone City is located in eastern part of Sinnoh region. Trainers who beat the city's Gym (a -type Gym) are awarded the Cobble Badge. Also located in Veilstone City is the Game Corner and the Veilstone Department Store.

This quaint city also includes a Pokémon Center, Team Galactic HQ, the Galactic Warehouse, Meteorites that will change the form of Deoxys, and the Prize Exchange. The prizes include Silk Scarf, Wide Lens, Zoom Lens, Metronome, and the TM68 and more TMs.

The road to get to the Gym Leader is not direct and there are several punching bags that the player character has to strategically push until the road is open to reach the Gym Leader.

Team Galactic's main base. The player must infiltrate it to rescue the three captured Lake Pokémon.

entities.description:
Bertha is a member of the Sinnoh Elite Four. She specializes in -type Pokémon.

Bertha is an aging woman, whose appearance and name resembles Agatha: they both have the same hairstyle and the suffix "tha" in their English names. Bertha wears a brown scarf, a white buttoned coat, a black skirt, long grey socks and black shoes.

Despite her humble and gentle demeanor, Bertha holds herself as a strong and enduring trainer. She knows when she's beaten and doesn't regret defeat.

Her Japanese name, Kikuno, may be derived from 崎嶇 (kiku, steep) or 国 (kuni, country). In either event, it may also come from Kikuko, Agatha's Japanese name, as both are elderly women who are part of their region's Elite Four lineup.

entities.description:
Mistralton City is a city located in the western part of Unova. The surrounding area is dominated by mountains and forestland, making it a rather difficult place to get to on foot. Chargestone Cave is to the south of the city, with Route 7 and Twist Mountain to the north.

Like many areas in the western part of the region, it has a cool climate and often rains. This city is unique as it is the only city in any of the Pokémon games to have a functional airport modeled in it, although it's more often used for transporting cargo to faraway regions and isn't often open to travelers.

The Pokémon Center is located in the east of the city. As well as the Poké Mart section stocking weather changing TMs, a man here can tell you what type of Hidden Power your Pokémon can learn.

To the right of the Pokémon Center is the house where the Move Family lives. Conveniently, both the Move Deleter and the Reminder girl are here. The reminder girl will help your Pokémon to relearn a move in exchange for one Heart Scale. Another girl here will give you advice on obtaining Heart Scales, telling you about a lady in the Cargo Service building, and also talking of a woman in Driftveil City who gives Heart Scales if you show her the right Pokémon.

entities.short_description: The Bell Tower, titled Tin Tower in the Generation II games, is a tall building in Ecruteak City in Johto. The player is required to have the Rainbow Wing to access the Bell Tower in and the remakes , allowing them them…
entities.description:
The Bell Tower, titled Tin Tower in the Generation II games, is a tall building in Ecruteak City in Johto. The player is required to have the Rainbow Wing to access the Bell Tower in and the remakes , allowing them them and some Kimono Girls to summon a level 40 Ho-Oh, at a stronger level 70 in and .

In , the Clear Bell is also required because it summons Suicune at the first floor of the Tin Tower. However, the player can get Ho-Oh to appear if they have caught the three Legendary Beasts and entered the Hall of Fame; the former methods cannot be worked around if receiving each of the Legendary Beasts through trading.

In the Generation IV remakes, if the player does not capture Ho-Oh on the first encounter, they are given another chance to after entering the Hall of Fame. Additionally, the remakes show a Rattata in the location preview, on the top right during morning and on the left side during the day and evening, while showing a Gastly during the night instead.

Kurt is a helper. When he tries to defeat the Team Rocket Grunt, he falls down the well, hurting his back in the process. He then asks the player to go down into the well in his place, and defeat the Team Rocket Grunts in order to rescue the Slowpokes.

entities.short_description: Nimbasa City is a location introduced in Generation V.
entities.description:
Nimbasa City is a location introduced in Generation V.

Nimbasa City is a vibrant city of entertainment located in the central part of Unova. There are three routes connecting to it: to the south of the city is Route 4 and the vast Desert Resort, to the west is Route 5, and to the east is Route 16.

At a population of 237, Nimbasa City is the most populous city in the Unova region and the second most populous city in the Pokémon world, after Kalos' Lumiose City and known as the city of leisure. This reputation has been gained thanks to large investment in this sector; many of the buildings are dedicated to entertainment and it only has two residential buildings. It wastes a lot of electricity causing Black City to conserve electricity.

The city boasts its own theme park with the Rondez-View Ferris Wheel. It has its own Gym, of which Elesa is the Gym Leader. Some other locations include the Big Stadium and Small Court, a Pokémon Center, and the Battle Subway, as well as being the home of the Pokémon Musical.

entities.short_description: Team Plasma is the antagonistic team in the Unova region and first appeared in Pokémon: Black & White. The player first meets them in Accumula Town giving a speech on releasing Pokémon.
entities.description:
Team Plasma is the antagonistic team in the Unova region and first appeared in Pokémon: Black & White. The player first meets them in Accumula Town giving a speech on releasing Pokémon.

They appear as a friendly organization that seeks to be equals with Pokémon; they encourage others to reevaluate their current relationships with Pokémon and considered how using them in battles is cruel. Leading the effort is an odd boy named N, who serves as King of Team Plasma. At the end of the first game, this is revealed to have been a front set up by Ghetsis, who wished to conquer the Unova region unopposed by tricking everyone into freeing their Pokémon.

In the second game, the remnants of Team Plasma have gone down to two separate routes. Those with kind hearts have united under the leadership of former member of the Seven Sages, Rood, and reside in a humble housing to care for neglected and abandoned Pokémon.

Those loyal to Ghetsis continue to serve him along with Colress and Zinzolin, hoping to once more conquer the Unova region. This time, Ghetsis' plan borders on total insanity by trying to bend the powers of the mightiest member of the Tao Trio to his whims.

Factory Head Thorton is the second Frontier Brain in the Sinnoh region. He is in charge of the Battle Factory.

Thorton is a pale, teal-eyed man with black slick hair, with the top being green. Unlike most people, his eyes are always half-shut. He wears a teal tie, which has a white button, over his black shirt with white sleeves. Thorton wears a teal belt, green shorts and black shoes. Thorton also has some gadgets, which he usually keeps in a spare container around his waist.

Thorton is a knowledgeable analyst who is confident in his abilities and analyses. He has even invented a machine just to analyse the possibilities of the player character winning against him. However, he acknowledges and appreciates the friendship between Pokémon and people, so he usually tells the player character not to care about his machine's results too seriously.

He is mostly the same with Noland of the Hoenn region, his Pokémon are random. When rematched, it's highly troublesome, because the player character almost never notices a type frequency, which is the clue of the seventh set. He usually has at least one Legendary Pokémon.

entities.short_description: Sandgem Town is a town found in Pokémon Diamond and Pearl and is located in the Sinnoh region. It is the second town you come to in the game, the first being Twinleaf Town. Sandgem Town has two houses, one of them being…
entities.description:
Sandgem Town is a town found in Pokémon Diamond and Pearl and is located in the Sinnoh region. It is the second town you come to in the game, the first being Twinleaf Town. Sandgem Town has two houses, one of them being the character's other rival's house. It has the Pokémon Lab (which is run by Professor Rowan), a Pokémon Center, and a Poké Mart. This town will be very useful after you beat the Elite Four and get the National Dex. Once you get the National Dex, you can go to the house directly below the Pokémon Center. This is Dawn/Lucas's house. Talk to their little sister, and she will tell you where a Pokémon Swarm is.

{|border="1" cellspacing="1" cellpadding="1" width="75%"

Once you reach Sandgem Town, Prof. Rowan's assistant will greet you and take you inside the lab. Just as you are going to enter the lab, your friend comes out and bumps you. Your friend will say that Prof. Rowan isn't as scary as he thought before he speeds off. You head inside and talk to Prof. Rowan. Prof. Rowan will ask you to complete the encyclopedia Pokédex. (If you refuse, he will reply "..." several times until you agree.) Prof. Rowan's kid will be holding a Pokémon that you and your friend did not choose. If you and your rival choose Turtwig and Chimchar, he/she will choose Piplup.

Head outside the lab and Prof. Rowan's kid will show you around the town. He/She will show you the Pokémon Center and the Pokémon Mart. Then he/she tells you to inform your Mom that you are going out for an adventure in order to complete the Pokédex before he/she runs away to Route 202. Because the kid don't allow you to pass Route 202, you head back to Twinleaf Town to inform your Mom about your adventure.

entities.description:
The Silph Corporation is a company based in the Kanto region, whose aim is to provide tools essential to Pokémon Trainers: namely, Poké Balls, Technical Machines, and a rare Poké Ball known as the Master Ball. It is perhaps known best for its invention of a device that enables invisible Pokémon to become visible, known as the Silph Scope. Their primary base of operations lies in Saffron City, and are rumored to own the entire Poké Mart franchise in the Pokémon World. The President of Silph Co. is an elderly man. During Generation IV, the Silph Co. logo was introduced in the form of a statue situated in the main foyer. Additionally, if the player defeats Blue, a scientist will reward the player with a Lapras.

You can only receive those Pokémon after defeating Red and you can only receive one of those Pokémon

In Pokémon Sword and Shield, the Normal Uniform's sponsor logo is the Silph Co. logo. This makes it the only company to sponsor a Galarian Gym (albeit a minor league one) that doesn't offer any Poké Jobs.

entities.name: Flint
entities.short_description: Flint, occasionally flintstone (SiO2), is a sedimentary cryptocrystalline form of the mineral quartz, categorized as the variety of chert that occurs in chalk or marly limestone. Historically, flint was widely used to…
entities.description:
Flint, occasionally flintstone (SiO2), is a sedimentary cryptocrystalline form of the mineral quartz, categorized as the variety of chert that occurs in chalk or marly limestone. Historically, flint was widely used to make stone tools and start fires.

Flint occurs chiefly as nodules and masses in sedimentary rocks, such as chalks and limestones. Inside the nodule, flint is usually dark grey or black, green, white, or brown in colour, and has a glassy or waxy appearance. A thin, oxidised layer on the outside of the nodules is usually different in colour, typically white and rough in texture. The nodules can often be found along streams and beaches.

When flint is broken or chipped, the pieces have sharp edges, making it useful as cutting tools, such as knife blades and scrapers. The use of flint to make stone tools dates back more than three million years; flint's extreme durability has made it possible to accurately date its use over this time. Flint is one of the primary materials used to define the Stone Age.

During the Stone Age, access to flint was so important for survival that people would travel or trade long distances to obtain the stone. Grime's Graves was an important source of flint traded across Europe.  Flint Ridge in Ohio was another important source of flint, and Native Americans extracted flint from hundreds of quarries along the ridge. This "Ohio Flint" was traded across the eastern United States, and has been found as far west as the Rocky Mountains and south around the Gulf of Mexico.

When struck against steel, flint will produce enough sparks to ignite a fire with the correct tinder, or gunpowder used in weapons, namely the flintlock firing mechanism. Although it has been superseded in these uses by different processes (the percussion cap), or materials (ferrocerium), "flint" has lent its name as generic term for a fire starter.

Brycen, also known by his title Ice Mask, is the former Gym Leader of Icirrus City's Gym who specializes in -types Pokémon, and is the seventh gym to be challenged by the player character. Brycen made his debut in Pokémon Black and White. He will award the player character the Freeze Badge if they defeat him.

Brycen is a muscular man with blue eyes and teal hair. He wears a blue mask around his eyes, with a "tail" with a purple ribbon. Brycen wears a blue mantle with white hexagonal features, which covers his left arm and torso. Brycen also wears black pants and azure shoes.

Competent and serious, Brycen is a trainer of multiple talents particularly in battling and acting. Judging by his style and battle stances, Brycen may be a tribute to the Shaolin Monks and superheroes.

In his youth, however, he used to be cocky and reckless until he got a severe injury in one instance, thus changing his overall attitude.

Professor Felina Ivy is a character appearing in Pokémon the Series: The Beginning, who is a Professor from the Orange Islands.

Professor Ivy is a tall, light skinned woman with purple hair and a rather sleepy look in her brown eyes. When first seen, she wears a navy-blue one-piece swimsuit before donning her lab coat. She later wore her lab coat and necklace with a salmon top, a black skirt and pink shoes.

Professor Ivy is friendly, and has a seemingly mellow disposition. When in discussions about science, she tends to get carried away. Ivy is very dedicated to her research, breeding Pokémon and studying the regional and climate differences in Pokémon physiology. She allowed Brock to study under her while Ash and Misty begin their Orange Island adventures. It's never explained what she taught Brock or what happened between them before he left her research center.

Ash and Misty allowed Brock to study under Professor Ivy while they went on another Pokémon adventure through the Orange Islands. Over the time of Brock's absence, his character was replaced with Tracey Sketchit, a Pokémon Watcher and artist.

entities.description:
Ursula is a character appearing in the Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl, who is a rival of Dawn.

Ursula has cherry-colored eyes and dark cream pink hair tied in lavender ribbons. Her casual wear is a white long sleeved mini-coat held by another identical ribbon on her chest, a sky blue dress that reaches her knees, white pantyhose, and white low-heel pumps. Her regular contest outfit is a long, black shirt with puffy cuffs, a black choker in her neck, a long dark red skirt and black flats. In the Grand Festival, she wore a different choker, a periwinkle dress-coat held by a large white ribbon, with a violet top and a soft blue skirt underneath.

Ursula is a determined Coordinator. However, she is also arrogant, viewing her rivals as underneath herself and as obstacles. When she loses a round, she dismisses her opponents off as that they won purely by luck.

Ursula competed in the Wallace Cup, but failed to win past the first round. Before entering Chocovine Town's Contest, she earned three ribbons.

Roxie is the -type Gym Leader at Virbank City's Gym in Unova.

Roxie is a medium height, slim young girl with bright blue eyes, pale skin and long layered white hair tied in a high, spiky ponytail with a purple and blue cherry bobble. Roxie wears a loose sky blue dress with magenta-purple stripes over a black vest top and long knee-length black boots with teal platforms. Roxie is often seen with her symbolic black bass with purple stripes.

Punkish and rebellious, Roxie befits the stereotype of a typical Rocker. She is a passionate musician, who enjoys her band very much. Interestingly, her choice of Pokémon type suites various real life rock songs and themes for example "Poison" sung by famous singer, Alice Cooper.

She is shown to be rather determined and stubborn, as she was adamant in forcing her father to do his job as a sailor, and when she knew that he quit his sailor job to venture into Pokéstar Studios, she furiously blurted out "idiot" for eight times. However, she still cares for her father, as she comforted him after knowing that he was mocked by the audience for his movie.

entities.description:
Littleroot Town is a location introduced in Generation III.

Littleroot Town is a main small town located in the southern area of Hoenn, and is surrounded by a thick forest. This is the player's hometown, where they move into and begin their journey in , , and the remakes . If the player is a boy, their house is on the left, but if they are a girl, their house is on the right. In either case, the second floor of the house is where their room is located. The other house is inhabited by Professor Birch, his child (who is the player's rival), and his wife.

Aside from the two houses, the only other location in Littleroot Town is Professor Birch's Laboratory. Unlike previous games in the Pokémon core series, the player does not receive his or her first Pokémon in the lab. Instead, when Birch is chased by a wild Poochyena (Zigzagoon in Emerald) in Route 101, just outside of Littleroot Town, the player has to select their first partner Pokémon from Birch's bag to battle the wild Pokémon with. After Birch is rescued, the player goes with him into the laboratory, back in Littleroot Town, where he gives them the Hoenn Pokédex. After this, the player's Mom gives them a pair of Running Shoes, though only in the original Generation III games.

Much later, when the player has completed the Hoenn Pokédex in Pokémon Emerald Version (excluding Jirachi and Deoxys), and has obtained the National Pokédex from Professor Birch, he allows them to select one of the starter Pokèmon from Johto: Chikorita, Cyndaquil, or Totodile.

entities.name: Delia Ketchum
entities.short_description: Delia Ketchum, also known as Mrs. Ketchum, is a character appearing in the anime series and the mother of Ash Ketchum.
entities.description:
Delia Ketchum, also known as Mrs. Ketchum, is a character appearing in the anime series and the mother of Ash Ketchum.

Delia is a slender woman with fair skin and brown eyes. In contrast to her son (who has messy and spiky black hair), Delia has smooth red hair that she commonly keeps in a ponytail with a green scrunchie. She usually wears a pink short-sleeved jacket with a yellow undershirt, a purple skirt, and light green shoes, though her outfits vary. Starting with the Sun and Moon series, Delia's skirt is light blue with an indigo stripe and the color of her shoes were changed to white.

When doing housework, Delia wears a light yellow T-shirt, a pink apron, blue jeans (later changed to a green dress), and orange shoes. She sometimes wears a straw hat and the purple skirt from her usual outfit, however.

When she watched Ash compete in the Indigo and Johto Leagues, Delia wore a blue dress with a white short-sleeved jacket, single red bead pendant necklace along with matching shoes. During her vacation in Alola, she wore an orange strapless dress with pink circles on the chest, a pink belt with a gold buckle around her waist, a pink flower, and white frills. She also wore a white coat over her dress, along with a matching sun hat and pink sandals.

Buck is a character first appearing in Pokémon Diamond Version and Pokémon Pearl Version.

Buck is a young man with red hair tied into a ponytail, with a yellow stripe. He has red eyes. He wears a red T-shirt with a black design, black baggy shorts and black shoes with red outlines.

He can join the player during an event in Pokémon Diamond, Pearl and Platinum. He asks the player to join him to the top of Stark Mountain because he underestimated the strength of the wild Pokémon located there. He then follows the player around, keeping the player's Pokémon healthy. The player must help him find the 'treasure' of Stark Mountain. After getting to the room where the treasure, and later Heatran, is found, he takes the treasure which appears as a stone in the games. Afterward, he can be found in his grandfather's house in the Fight Area where he is told to return the stone to its rightful place. Later, he can be found in Sinnoh's Battle Tower competing against the player. He specializes in Pokémon that have high Defense/Special Defense capabilities.

Most regions have only one Pokémon Professor, who typically gives a first partner Pokémon and a Pokédex to new Pokémon Trainers for their journey, especially the protagonists. A Pokémon Professor usually wears a white lab coat, just like Scientists. Most Pokémon Professors are elderly.

According to legend, this tower is home to the legendary Pokémon, Ho-Oh.

The Burned Tower used to be as tall as the Bell Tower before it got burned down in a mysterious fire 150 years prior to the events of Pokémon Gold, Silver, Crystal and their remakes. The legendary beasts: Raikou, Entei and Suicune can be encountered for the first time in the basement, after which they flee. The name Fennel comes from "fennel", a type of flowering plant species.

entities.short_description: Breeding is a mechanic introduced in Generation II that involves choosing two Pokémon owned by the player to send to the local region's Day Care in the hopes that the pair will produce an Egg. This is a useful technique…
entities.description:
Breeding is a mechanic introduced in Generation II that involves choosing two Pokémon owned by the player to send to the local region's Day Care in the hopes that the pair will produce an Egg. This is a useful technique to raise Pokémon with unusual attributes, such as elevated Attack, Defense, Speed, etc. compared to members of the same species on a similar level. Pokémon that are hatched from Eggs can have access to stronger attacks earlier than normal, such as learning a parent's TM or HM move. Some Pokémon, like Pichu, can learn a move the parents would never learn, such as Volt Tackle if one of the parents are holding a special item, such as the Light Ball in Pichu's case.

The locations of the Day Care center depends on the versions of the game.

When the Day Care Center alerts you of a new Egg, you must move around to hatch it, such as through walking or riding the Bicycle. You must have an empty slot on your team to accept the Egg. The Day Care center will keep it if you did not do so. Every Egg has a special number of steps required to hatch it.

Nando is a character appearing in Pokémon the Series: Diamond and Pearl, who is a friend and rival of Ash and Dawn.

Nando is a tall young man with light skin, shoulder-length black hair, and blue eyes, one of which is always covered by his hair. His usual outfit consists of a green hat and a green cape held together by a red gem and blue cravat, over a blue vest, off-white shirt, gray trousers, and black boots. He always wears a brown shoulder bag, and carries a golden harp shaped like a Mew.

Nando is a calm, gentle, and kind-hearted individual. He is very polite and always speaks in a formal manner, even giving commands to his Pokémon during battles in the form of polite requests. He has a love of music, and likes to play his harp for others.

Due to his relaxed nature, he is rarely fazed or upset by anything, even being falsely arrested for a crime he did not commit. However, he sometimes gets excited during particularly intense Pokémon battles. When asked if he prefers Gym Battles or Contests he says he likes both.

entities.name: Distortion World
entities.short_description: The is an alternate dimension into which Giratina was banished by Arceus. It can be accessed from two locations in the Sinnoh region, Spear Pillar atop Mt. Coronet, as well as Turnback Cave.
entities.description:
The is an alternate dimension into which Giratina was banished by Arceus. It can be accessed from two locations in the Sinnoh region, Spear Pillar atop Mt. Coronet, as well as Turnback Cave.

The Distortion World serves primarily as a prison for Giratina, in which the Pokémon is able to roam freely throughout it. The Distortion World is made up of a multitude of levitating islands, and due to the unusual nature of it, many laws of physics can be disobeyed. Namely, the player can move at angles which would normally be impossible in the real world, which is not limited to surfing.

The Distortion World first appears in , where Cyrus summons both Dialga and Palkia to Spear Pillar, in an attempt to create the perfect world. Sensing the disturbance occurring, Giratina conjures up a portal to the Reverse World, snatching Cyrus from Spear Pillar. The Player and Cynthia venture down after them, and have to maneuver through a series of levels with the assistance of Mesprit, Azelf and Uxie. Cyrus is staying at the Distortion World, never to see Lucas/Dawn or Cynthia again.

The Reverse World is the anime-only counterpart to the Distortion World. Despite this, its features vary differently to the game counterpart. In the movie Giratina and the Sky Warrior, the Reverse World is depicted as a large expanse of buildings constructed bilaterally to one another. There are also various other features not included within the game version. Namely, there are a multitude of bubbles floating around the Reverse World, which portray events happening in the real world. These bubbles are poisonous, however. In the Reverse World, there are also ice pillars scattered across the vast expanse, which serve mainly as "support pillars" for the real world. To this effect, when Zero goes in a frenzied rage, destroying pillars left, right and center, it causes adverse effects in the real world.

entities.description:
Viridian Forest is a location introduced in Generation I.

Viridian Forest is a location in the Kanto region that connects Viridian City to Pewter City. It is a winding maze of trees and grass, and Viridian Forest is home to some of the weaker -type Pokémon, such as Caterpies and Weedles. On occasion, a Pikachu can be found here. A few Bug Catchers can be fought here as well.

In the Generation II games, Viridian Forest had been deforested, meaning that Wild Pokémon can no longer be encountered here. It is just a small maze with tiny trees and some items to obtain. This decision was reversed with the remakes Pokémon HeartGold Version and Pokémon SoulSilver Version, where some Pokémon Trainers can be battled and wild Pokémon can be encountered.

The Battle Zone is a sub-region on an island off the northeast of mainland Sinnoh and is home to the Battle Tower, where the player character can get Battle Points, like in Hoenn's Battle Frontier. The Battle Zone's people do not consider the sub-region to be a part of Sinnoh.

The Battle Zone is home to three major settlements, the Fight Area, the Survival Area and the Resort Area. Sinnoh's Battle Tower}}Battle Frontier}} is also located in the Fight Area. In the Battle Zone, there is a facility called the Fight Area which serves as the entrance to the Battle Tower in Pokémon Diamond and Pearl. In the Survival Area, the player character can rematch Sinnoh Gym Leaders in Pokémon Platinum.

Battle Park in Diamond and Pearl or Battle Frontier in Platinum is located northeast of Fight Area. Similarly to Emerald, Battle Points are won from battles and can be exchanged for goods and move tutoring services.

Nearby the Survival Area lies the Stark Mountain an active volcano. This is where the legendary Heatran can be caught.

The is location that holds several rare Pokémon that can't be captured anywhere else. It acts as a sanctuary for rare Pokémon and the player can participate in a timed game. Since it is primarily a sanctuary, trainers cannot battle in the Safari Zone. There are three Safari Zones: one in Kanto located in Fuchsia City, one in Hoenn located west of Lilycove City, and one in Johto located west of Cianwood City (HGSS only).

Besides being a Pokémon sanctuary, the Safari Zone offer a game, where a Trainer can go in for a limited time and capture as many Pokémon they can with Safari Balls. Upon paying the fee for entering, the player receives 30 Safari Balls and in most Safari Zones can walk up to 500 steps. In most games, the player can throw bait, a rock, or a Safari Ball at wild Pokémon.

entities.name: Diamond
entities.short_description: Diamond is a mineral form of the element carbon with its atoms arranged in a crystal structure called diamond cubic. Diamond is a tasteless, odorless, strong, brittle solid, a poor conductor of electricity, colorless in…
entities.description:
Diamond is a mineral form of the element carbon with its atoms arranged in a crystal structure called diamond cubic. Diamond is a tasteless, odorless, strong, brittle solid, a poor conductor of electricity, colorless in pure form, and insoluble in water. Another solid form of carbon known as graphite is the chemically stable form of carbon at room temperature and pressure, but diamond is metastable and converts to it at a negligible rate under those conditions. Diamond has the highest hardness and thermal conductivity of any natural material, properties that are used in major industrial applications such as cutting and polishing tools.

Because the arrangement of atoms in diamond is extremely rigid, few types of impurity can contaminate it (two exceptions are boron and nitrogen). Small numbers of defects or impurities—about one per million of lattice atoms—can color a diamond blue (boron), yellow (nitrogen), brown (defects), green (radiation exposure), purple, pink, orange, or red. Diamond also has a very high refractive index and a relatively high optical dispersion.

Most natural diamonds have ages between 1 billion and 3.5 billion years. Most were formed at depths between 150 and 250 kilometres (93 and 155 mi) in the Earth's mantle, although a few have come from as deep as 800 kilometres (500 mi). Under high pressure and temperature, carbon-containing fluids dissolved various minerals and replaced them with diamonds. Much more recently (hundreds to tens of million years ago), they were carried to the surface in volcanic eruptions and deposited in igneous rocks known as kimberlites and lamproites.

Synthetic diamonds can be grown from high-purity carbon under high pressures and temperatures or from hydrocarbon gases by chemical vapor deposition (CVD). Natural and synthetic diamonds are most commonly distinguished using optical techniques or thermal conductivity measurements.

Birth Island is one of the Sevii Islands and is the home to the Mythical Pokémon Deoxys in FireRed, LeafGreen and Emerald.

To get to Birth Island, the player character needs the Aurora Ticket event item. This item is sometimes called Nine Island because it is the ninth in the chain of islands which make up the Sevii Islands. The player character can go here via the Seagallop dock in Pokémon FireRed and LeafGreen and the S.S Tidal in Pokémon Emerald. Once the player character arrives on Birth Island, they have to rotate a stone triangle positioned in the center until it glows bright red. However, if the player character stops moving the triangle, it will immediately reset and the player character will have to begin again. When it glows red, Deoxys will appear before the player character (Attack Forme in Pokémon FireRed, Speed Forme in Pokémon Emerald and Defense Forme in Pokémon LeafGreen).

Nacrene City is an old city in eastern Unova, located between Route 3 and Pinwheel Forest. Its peculiar cityscape was made up of abandoned textile factories and century-old warehouses until enterprising young artists began using them as studios. This was essentially the beginning of the city, and it is still known as the city of art to this day, attracting many creative artists and poets. An abandoned railroad lies in the south of the city.

The second Gym of the region, which doubles up as a fossil museum, is found here. There are a few other notable places to visit too; such as Café Warehouse, which has a Soda Pop special on Wednesdays; Loblolly's studio, where Loblolly designs furniture for you to use in the Dream World; and a warehouse shop selling battle items.

When the Player first arrives in the city, Cheren is waiting to talk to them about the Gym and gives advice about how to face it. However, when the Player heads to the Gym they find N, who voices his opinions on Pokémon before challenging the Player to a battle.

After N is defeated, the Player can go inside and get a tour of the museum, guided by Lenora's husband, Professor Hawes. Amongst the curiosities are a Dragon Skull, an ancient round stone that was buried in the desert, and a meteor that has a space virus attached to it. The latter can be used for changing Deoxys's form. Fossils can also be restored here by the woman behind the right counter.

entities.short_description: Pokémon Ruby Version and Pokémon Sapphire Version are 2002 role-playing video games developed by Game Freak and published by The Pokémon Company and Nintendo for the Game Boy Advance. They are the first installments in…
entities.description:
Pokémon Ruby Version and Pokémon Sapphire Version are 2002 role-playing video games developed by Game Freak and published by The Pokémon Company and Nintendo for the Game Boy Advance. They are the first installments in the third generation of the Pokémon video game series, also known as the "advanced generation". After years of Nintendo being the sole publisher of the franchise in all regions, The Pokémon Company co-published the games for the first time since the establishment of the joint-owned company in 1998. They were first released in Japan in late 2002, and internationally in 2003. Pokémon Emerald, a third version, was released two years later in each region. Remakes of the two games, titled Pokémon Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire, were released for the Nintendo 3DS worldwide in November 2014, exactly twelve years to the date of the original Ruby and Sapphire release date, with the exception of Europe, where it released a week later.

The gameplay is mostly unchanged from the previous games; the player controls the main character from an overhead perspective, and the controls are largely the same as those of previous games. As with previous games, the main objectives are to catch all of the Pokémon in the games and defeat the Elite Four and the Pokémon League Champion; also like their predecessors, the games' main subplot involves the player character defeating a criminal organization that attempts to take over the region. New features, such as double battles, Pokémon abilities, Pokémon Contests, and 135 new Pokémon were added. Owing to the increased capabilities of the Game Boy Advance, four players may be connected to each other at a time instead of the previous limit of two. Additionally, the games can be connected to an e-Reader or other third-generation Pokémon games.

Ruby and Sapphire received mostly positive reviews; praise was given to the new features and Pokémon designs, though critics were divided in their assessment of the games, especially on the gameplay and graphics. Most of the complaints focused on gameplay not changing much in relation to previous generations. With over 16.22 million copies sold, they were a commercial success and became the best-selling game for the Game Boy Advance; however, the games sold less than previous generations with Red and Blue having sold nearly 31 million units worldwide, and Gold and Silver selling over 23.10 million units.

To the east of the city, there is a ship that can take Trainers to Castelia City. And to the south, lies the Virbank Complex.

entities.name: Pokémon Center
entities.short_description: A Pokémon Center is a type of location introduced in Generation I.
entities.description:
A Pokémon Center is a type of location introduced in Generation I.

A Pokémon Center is used mainly to replenish the HP, PP, and any status condition of the Pokémon in the player's party, free of charge. They are located in nearly every town and city. The Pokémon at a Pokémon Center are cured by a Pokémon Center Lady in the lobby, with a machine behind the counter. A Pokémon Center can typically be identified from its red roof. Pokémon Centers have a PC, which stores the player's Pokémon outside of their party, although they can also deposit Pokémon into the PC or withdraw a Pokémon from there if their party has an open slot.

Every Pokémon Center in a game of the core series generally has no difference in layout or appearance from one another. Pokémon Centers have a red or an orange roof, depending on the game. They are inscribed with the word "Poké" in games of the first three generations. Since Generation III, every Pokémon Center has a Poké Ball symbol on its roof, which would replace "Poké" outright by Generation IV, as well as automatic doors instead of regular ones.

From Generations V to VIII, each Pokémon Center also has a Poké Mart, which is integrated within every Pokémon Center of Unova, Kalos, Alola, and Galar.

Lorelei is a lithe and curvy woman, whose hair has two pigtails and a ponytail. She wears a pair of glasses, with her eyes being hazel-colored.

In Generation I, Lorelei wears a blue jacket, a red shirt, and a black pencil skirt reveals her legs. She also wears a pair of black high heeled shoes. Lorelei has violet hair.

In Pokémon FireRed Version and Pokémon LeafGreen Version, Lorelei wears a black sleeveless shirt, a purple pencil mini skirt, black high heels and a golden bracelet around her right arm. Lorelei also has red hair.

entities.name: Ability
entities.short_description: An |Tokusei}}, called Special Ability in Pokémon the Series, is a mechanic that was introduced in Generation III.
entities.description:
An |Tokusei}}, called Special Ability in Pokémon the Series, is a mechanic that was introduced in Generation III.

Abilities are various powers or characteristics possessed by each Pokémon. Abilities are activated automatically in battle, and some have shown to have use outside of battle. There are many types of Abilities. Some Abilities are exclusive to certain Pokémon and their evolutions, while others are known by many Pokémon. Generation V introduces a certain type of Ability, Hidden Abilities, which certain Pokémon have depending on where they are encountered, including certain Gift Pokémon.

While several species of Pokémon can know only one Ability, many of them can have one of a few Abilities, such as Gligar, which can have either Hyper Cutter or Sand Veil. The evolved form of certain Pokémon can have a different Ability than its basic form. In Generation III, Generation IV, and , the Ability of a newborn Pokémon is decided randomly, regardless of the Abilities of each of its parents. This was rectified in , in which the hatched Pokémon has an eighty percent chance of inheriting the Ability of its mother. Additionally, there is a sixty percent chance that the Hidden Ability of the newborn Pokémon is inherited by its mother, but only if both its mother and father are part of the same egg group. As of Generation VI, the father can pass a Hidden Ability onward if its partner is a Ditto.

Since its introduction, Abilities have appeared in most games of the core series, as well as and even spinoff games. Abilities do not return in , presumably because it is based on the Generation I game , which released prior to the introduction of Abilities, or because it is based on Pokémon GO, another game in which Abilities do not appear. Although as well as do not feature Abilities, they are still determined within the game's data, for if Pokémon had been traded over from a different game in the core series.

entities.name: Lumiose City
entities.short_description: Lumiose City is a location introduced in .
entities.description:
Lumiose City is a location introduced in .

Lumiose City is the capital and largest city of the Kalos region. It is a big, circular city divided into two halves: the North Boulevard and South Boulevard, each having two avenues. Plazas are located in the innermost part of Lumiose City. There are alleyways that branch from the boulevards and always lead to a dead end, while those across the avenues are long. In the North Boulevard, some of the alleys feature Pokémon Trainers. Lumiose City has several cafés, most of which are optional to visit.

Being a large city, players can easily get around on Roller Skates, a bicycle, or even by doing a Poké Ride on a Gogoat. Using a Bicycle does not change the background music. Lumiose City also has its own taxi service and a train station. Lumiose City's vast size makes it easy to get lost, and its transportation options let you reach your destination directly.

Lumiose City also has its own Style system, where the player can do various tasks to increase Style and receive benefits based on how much Style they have, especially discounts.

entities.description:
Bruno is the second Elite Four member in the Kanto region and the third Elite Four member in the Johto region. He specializes in -types, and occasionally uses Onix as well.

Bruno is tall and muscular man. He has long black hair, tied in a thick ponytail, which dangles down his back to his shoulder blades and longish thick sideburns. He has small dark eyes with prominent eyebrows, a small nose and a square jaw. He wears white trousers with a tattered waist and ankles that are held up by a black belt, shirtless, unshod, and has black spiked bands on his wrists and ankles.

Stolid yet intimidating, Bruno is a character who represents his preferred type very accurately indeed. With great belief in his training, his impressive physique no doubt came from many years of training.

His English name, Bruno, may come from "brutal" or "brawn".

entities.short_description: Ritchie is a friend of Ash Ketchum and one of his oldest rivals.
entities.description:
Ritchie is a friend of Ash Ketchum and one of his oldest rivals.

Ritchie has brown hair and blue eyes. He wears a teal short-sleeve shirt with light yellow trim and a silver zipper, a dark teal vest with a light green collar, a black belt with a silver buckle, teal pants with light yellow pockets, dark blue and indigo sneakers with red dots, dark blue fingerless gloves with aqua borders, and a purple cap with a light yellow band and red buttons.

Ritchie has a calm and sensible personality. He is very like Ash, he loves his Pokémon and can do anything to save them. He befriends people easily. He is cheerful and gets competitive only in battle.

Like Ash, he too is friendly with his Pokémon. He is also a person who plays a fair battle, shown that when Ash didn't come in time for their battle, he insisted everyone to wait. He could have been the winner, but he decided to wait instead. He did that because he believes in a fair battle, and he didn't want to be a winner without even battling.

entities.description:
Flannery is the Gym Leader at Lavaridge Town's Gym in the Hoenn region. She had only recently become the town's Gym Leader at the time of the player's challenge and specializes in using -type Pokémon. Flannery has an unnamed grandfather who was formerly the Gym Leader of Lavaridge Town, so Flannery likely became his successor.

Flannery is a slender, medium height girl with long, straight crimson red hair that is tied up in a high, spiky ponytail with a blue band with a side fringe at the front, and crimson red eyes.

She wears a short black T-shirt with a red fire emblem on it, exposing her belly button, plain light blue jeans with a red belt, and black and gray colored shoes. Flannery is shown with pink hair in her overworld sprite. Her overworld sprite in was edited from to have her side fringe partially cover her right eye, consistent with her battle sprite.

She wears a red bandeau with yellow flames, exposing her belly button, and a black sleeveless tie front crop top over it. She also has on blue flared light blue jeans with red Xs down the sides with a white karate belt. Her shoes are colored as black and red.

entities.name: Morrison
entities.short_description: Morrison is one of Ash's friends. He was defeated in the Hoenn Tournament by Ash.
entities.description:
Morrison is one of Ash's friends. He was defeated in the Hoenn Tournament by Ash.

Morrison is a chubby light-skinned boy with tied-up orange hair, small black eyes, and wears a red and orange samurai-like attire.

Morrison is lively and extremely competitive. He has a liking for sandwiches.

Morrison dropped a rice ball when Ash caught it. Morrison went to get it, but bashed into a tree, and just as he was to take the rice ball, May's Munchlax ate it. Ignoring that, Morrison introduced himself to them, as well as Max and Brock. Morrison explained he was a participant for the Hoenn League, which sparked Ash's interest. As Morrison and Ash expressed their desires to become Pokémon Masters, they started to argue with one another. Morrison battled with his Beldum against Pikachu. Despite knowing only one move, Beldum and Pikachu knocked each other simultaneously, ending the battle in a draw. Morrison continued to argue, showing he had seven badges, but Brock reminded him the League would start in two months. Ash showed that he had all the badges, causing Morrison to dash away.

entities.name: AZ
entities.short_description: AZ is a character appearing in , and later Pokémon Legends: Z-A. He is a former king in Kalosian history.
entities.description:
AZ is a character appearing in , and later Pokémon Legends: Z-A. He is a former king in Kalosian history.

Lysandre believes him to be a descendant of the original AZ, who built the Ultimate Weapon, but he is in fact the very same AZ.

In Pokémon Legends: Z-A, AZ now runs a hotel named Hotel Z in Lumiose City, before later passing away in the same game.

AZ is often depicted as an extremely tall man, standing over 9 feet (3 meters) tall in height, which is a side effect after activating the Ultimate Weapon. AZ carries a heavy, time-worn presence—one shaped by age, endurance, and a weight of history that clings to every aspect of his being. His facial expression is stern and deeply worn, marked by heavy lines and a downturned mouth that suggest sorrow held long and rarely voiced. His eyes are shadowed and intense, perpetually tired yet unwavering, conveying grief, regret, and an unrelenting sense of responsibility. Long white hair spills freely from beneath his worn knit cap, cascading past his shoulders in thick, untamed strands that frame his face like a mantle of time itself, emphasizing both his age and isolation. His posture is slightly hunched yet steady, burdened more by memory than by weakness; whether kneeling or standing, he appears grounded and resolute. He is tall and powerfully built, standing over 9 feet (3 meters) tall in height, which is a side effect after activating the Ultimate Weapon. Though his stature feels subdued—not diminished, but weighed down by centuries of loss rather than physical frailty.

entities.name: Twinleaf Town
entities.short_description: Twinleaf Town is a town introduced in the Generation IV games.
entities.description:
Twinleaf Town is a town introduced in the Generation IV games.

Twinleaf Town is a small and quaint town located the Sinnoh region. It is the home of the player and their rival in , , and the remakes . Twinleaf Town has four houses, and the player's house is located in the southeast corner while their rival's house is located in the northwest corner. The town has a small lake at the very bottom, and it is also the nearest town to Lake Verity. There are two small gardens near the entry with flowers growing. Twinleaf Town is surrounded by trees, fencing in the town except for an opening at the north.

It lacks a Pokémon Lab, which is present in starting locations of previous games in the core series. Twinleaf Town is also the first starting town where the player does not receive their first partner Pokémon.

entities.name: Clemont
entities.short_description: Clemont is the Gym Leader at Lumiose City's Gym in the Kalos region. He specializes in -type Pokémon. He likes science and inventing new devices. He is the older brother of Bonnie.
entities.description:
Clemont is the Gym Leader at Lumiose City's Gym in the Kalos region. He specializes in -type Pokémon. He likes science and inventing new devices. He is the older brother of Bonnie.

Clemont is a short and skinny young boy with fair skin, gray eyes (in contrast to his anime counterpart, who has blue eyes), and messy medium-length bright yellow hair with a lightning-bolt shaped tuft on top. Outfit-wise, Clemont wears clothes that make him resemble a stereotypical geek or nerd. His outfit consists of large round glasses which obscure his eyes, black shoes with white soles, and a yellow-collared skin-tight blue jumpsuit with yellow stripes on the knees and bottom cuffs. Additionally, Clemont also sports a backpack-like cybernetic contraption (which he invented himself) on his back which is similar in appearance to Shuckle (or the hand of an Aipom) and Heliolisk. The contraption has two robotic extensions that Clemont uses to absorb solar and lunar energy - naturally, one appears to resemble the sun, while the other resembles the moon. The white moon-like contraption (known as the "Aipom Arm") is also used to grip and hold objects like an extra hand.

Clemont, despite being very young, is extremely intelligent with a passion for science, and is a child prodigy inventor. He is a very kind and respectful person who loves new challenges and gracefully accepts defeat, even thanking the player for showing him their battling skills. He isn't interested in becoming the most powerful trainer, but he loves to learn from the trainers he battles. He enjoys spending his time with his Pokémon. He also cares a lot about his little sister, Bonnie.

His Japanese name, Citron, it literally "citron", French for lemon. It also contains "tron," a suffix commonly used in the names of machines.

entities.name: Dark Cave
entities.short_description: The Dark Cave is a location introduced in Generation II.
entities.description:
The Dark Cave is a location introduced in Generation II.

The Dark Cave is a cave in Johto that neighbors three routes, each allowing access to a different part of the cave. The first entrance is located on Route 31, and it provides access to the southwest of the southern area. The second entrance is located south of Blackthorn City, and it allows the player to explore the northern area. The last entrance is located on Route 46, and it provides access to the southeast of the southern area. All three areas are on the same floor.

The location is named for its lack of visibility, requiring the player to use TM70 (Flash) to see their surroundings. Additionally, the player is also required to use HM04 (Strength) and HM06 (Rock Smash) to progress. Another feature of the Dark Cave is that it is the only area in Johto where the player can encounter wild Wobbuffets.

A Dunsparce swarm can sometimes occur in the Dark Cave. If the player has the Pokégear number of Hiker Anthony registered, he calls them if the swarm occurs.

entities.name: Ramos
entities.short_description: Ramos is the Gym Leader at Coumarine City's Gym that appears in Pokémon X and Pokémon Y. He specializes in -type Pokémon. He gives the player character the Plant Badge after they defeat him.
entities.description:
Ramos is the Gym Leader at Coumarine City's Gym that appears in Pokémon X and Pokémon Y. He specializes in -type Pokémon. He gives the player character the Plant Badge after they defeat him.

Ramos is an old, lanky man with pale skin, a hunchback, and perpetually closed eyes. Fittingly for his advanced age, he is also bald and has very little hair on his head, save for his eyebrows and his spiky white beard. For clothing, Ramos wears a rolled-up long-sleeved green shirt with black buttons and brown suspenders, gray work pants with a brown belt and a holster, and green boots with brown soles. To complete his outfit, he also wears an orange scarf, a green cap, and thick green gardening gloves. Additionally, he is always seen with some gardening scissors, keeping them close by.

Despite his age, Ramos is active and likes to tease people (though he can be calm and soothing when it's needed). However, his advanced age gives him vast intelligence and experience, which he often uses to lecture people and give them advice. Additionally, he also speaks with a very thick accent, which is represented by his dialogue referring to people as "yeh" and "yer."

The name Ramos comes from ramus (Latin for "branch") and "moss".

entities.short_description: Drasna is a member of Kalos' Elite Four. Out of all the Four, she is declared the kindest one. In the Battle Chateau, her class is Duchess, one of the highest of rank overall. Drasna specializes in -types.
entities.description:
Drasna is a member of Kalos' Elite Four. Out of all the Four, she is declared the kindest one. In the Battle Chateau, her class is Duchess, one of the highest of rank overall. Drasna specializes in -types.

Drasna is a woman who has dark blue hair with two pigtails. Drasna wears brown shirt with a yellow sash around her belly and also wears a striped dark red dress with rippled ends. Along with her dress and high-heeled shoes, she wears dragon accessories resembling dragon's teeth, which are connected by green and orange decorations.

Drasna is a very kind and happy person, always polite and pleased to meet anyone. When the player character first visits her, or even after the first visit, she will always give the them warm welcome. Although, she does show a sign of distress if she is defeated first out of all the Elite Four. But even when in loss, she remains happy to know that the player is a few steps closer to becoming the champion.

Uniquely, after the player character walks off, she waves swell goodbye and wishes them luck on defeating the Champion, Diantha.

entities.short_description: Professor Augustine Sycamore is the regional Pokémon professor of Pokémon X and Pokémon Y, situated in the Kalos region.
entities.description:
Professor Augustine Sycamore is the regional Pokémon professor of Pokémon X and Pokémon Y, situated in the Kalos region.

Professor Sycamore is a middle-aged man, with black, curly hair, bluish eyes and some facial hair under his ears. Sycamore wears a blue shirt, black trousers with a yellow belt (which has the buckle shaped like a circle), and also wears orange socks and brown trainers with gray stripes. Sycamore also wears a brown watch on his left arm and often wears with his white lab coat when he is not conducting field research.

Sycamore is a cheerful professor, who likes to help others. However, Sycamore's cheerfulness leads him sometimes to be naive and even oblivious of events and people. When seeing there is trouble abound, Sycamore becomes determined to conduct research to assist others. Sycamore was Lysandre's friend, but was shocked to see Lysandre is Team Flare's leader.

The last name Sycamore comes from the "sycamore" tree.

Lavaridge Town is a town located at the foothills of Mt. Chimney, accessible only by going down the Mt. Chimney via Jagged Pass other than soaring and flying. The Lavaridge Pokémon Center is connected to a hot spring, which is what Lavaridge Town is famous for all over the Hoenn region. An old lady in front of the hot springs gives the player character/protagonist a Pokémon Egg, which hatches into Wynaut. She will give you another Egg afterwards, which hatches into a Togepi. The Gym Leader of Lavaridge is Flannery, who uses -type Pokémon.

The hot springs are connected to the back of the Pokémon Center.

In , there is the home of a boy who will teach the move Mimic, but he will only do this once.

entities.short_description: Fortree City is a city located roughly between Mauville City and Lilycove City in the Hoenn Region.
entities.description:
Fortree City is a city located roughly between Mauville City and Lilycove City in the Hoenn Region.

Fortree City has a quite different design than any other city in the Pokémon World. The Fortree City has treehouses and several other wooden buildings. All the houses are built at a height from the ground so ladders are there to get to the houses. Wooden Bridges connect the Treehouse. It has a Pokémon Center, a Poké Mart, a Pokémon Gym and 6 to 7 houses (varies from game to game).

Fortree Gym is under the tutelage of Gym Leader Winona, who specializes in using -type Pokémon. The gym's layout revolves around the concept of rotating turnstile doors that will prevent the player from going backwards once the player goes through them. In order to reach Winona, the player is forced to navigate through these various gates and encounter numerous Trainers along the way.

Upon her defeat, Winona will award the player with the Feather Badge, which enables the player's Pokémon to use HM02 Fly outside of battle. Winona also grants the player the TM Aerial Ace.

entities.short_description: Lilycove City is a location introduced in Generation III.
entities.description:
Lilycove City is a location introduced in Generation III.

Lilycove City is a city located in the northeastern part of the Hoenn region, connected by Route 124 in the east and Route 121 in the west. However, the path to Route 124 is blocked by several Wailmers until the player character completes the Team Magma Hideout or Team Aqua Hideout at the northeast of Lilycove City.

Besides the villain hideout, Lilycove City has a variety of visitable areas. There is a Contest Hall, which hosts Master Rank Pokémon Contests in and all Contests in . To the east of the Contest Hall is Cove Lily Motel, which is empty until after Team Magma and Team Aqua flees Lilycove City, with staff members of Game Freak moving in by the time the player becomes the Pokémon Champion. To the north is the Lilycove Museum, which has art presented on display. To the east of the Lilycove Museum is the Lilycove Department Store, the largest store of the Hoenn region. To the east of the Lilycove Department Store is the home of the only Move Deleter in the Hoenn region, and to the south is the usual Pokémon Center, which is otherwise normal but has the Pokémon Center Ladies trio in that give rewards by record mixing with other players. To the southeast of the Move Deleter's House is the Pokémon Trainer Fan Club, where fans discuss popular Pokémon Trainers, including the player once they enter the Hall of Fame. At the southwest of Lilycove City is the Lilycove City Harbor, where the player can embark on the S.S. Tidal to travel to Slateport City, as well as the Battle Frontier in .

After the events at Seafloor Cavern, Lilycove City is affected by extremely harsh sunlight (in and ) or heavy rain (in and ) until the player battles Kyogre or Groudon at the Cave of Origin in Sootopolis City. The music is also replaced with the [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q4Vq0Fmz46s flood theme] or the [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bxwfl_-P2gI drought theme] while the respective weather is in effect, like with Mossdeep City, Sootopolis City, and Routes 124 through 131.

entities.description:
Mossdeep City is a location introduced in Generation III.

Mossdeep City is where Steven Stone lives. To get to Mossdeep, the player needs to Surf trough Route 124. The seventh Gym Leaders, Tate and Liza, are fought here in the Mossdeep City Gym, and both use -type Pokémon. After defeating the Gym in Ruby, Sapphire, Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire), Steven will give the player HM08 (Ruby and Sapphire)/HM07 (Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire) containing Dive.

In the northeast of the city is the Mossdeep Space Center. At one point, it is taken over by Team Magma for rocket fuel. After defeating Team Magma here in , Steven Stone gives the player HM08 (Dive).

After becoming the Champion, Steven leaves a Level 5 (Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald)/Level 1 (Omega Ruby and Alpha Sapphire) Beldum in his house, along with a letter.

entities.name: Rustboro City
entities.short_description: Rustboro City is a city in Hoenn. It is known for having the first Hoenn gym, with Roxanne specializing in -type Pokémon.
entities.description:
Rustboro City is a city in Hoenn. It is known for having the first Hoenn gym, with Roxanne specializing in -type Pokémon.

The city also contains the Devon Corporation, which makes items for people inside the game, for example the Pokémon Navigator, or the PokéNav for short. In addition, the Devon Corporation is also the area for Hoenn where fossils are reverted into living Pokémon.

The house beside the Pokémon Center is where the HM Cut can be gotten. You need to defeat the Gym leader Roxanne before you can use the HM Cut outside of battle. Go inside the Poké Mart, and talk to the guy in the suit and tie. He will give you the TM False Swipe, which will be useful once you get farther into the game and your Pokémon will be too strong to weaken a wild Pokémon without making it faint. Also, go to the Trainer's School, then talk to the teacher to get a Quick Claw. Then, go in the house northeast of the school. The kid wearing a blue hat will trade a Makuhita for your Slakoth, which will be useful for the gym battle.

It is connected to Petalburg City through the Petalburg Woods followed by a sea-side route from the south, connected to Fallarbor Town through Meteor Falls followed by a one-way trail from the north, and connected almost directly to Verdanturf Town through the Rusturf Tunnel from the east.

entities.short_description: Cherrygrove City is a location introduced in Generation II.
entities.description:
Cherrygrove City is a location introduced in Generation II.

Cherrygrove City is a small city located in Johto and the first city visited by the player in the region. Cherrygrove City has a population of about 12, and it is the second smallest city in Johto. This area is where the player battles their Rival for the first time.

When the player first visits Cherrygrove City, the Guide Gent, who is originally located near the town's east entrance, will offer them a tour of the city. The tour route includes the Pokémon Center, Poké Mart, the exit to Route 30, the coast, and the Guide Gent's house. After the tour is complete, the player receives the Map Card for their PokéGear. In Pokémon HeartGold and SoulSilver, the player instead receives the Running Shoes at this point, and the Guide Gent gives the Running Shoes when they are about to leave for Route 30.

entities.short_description: Goldenrod City is a location introduced in Generation II.
entities.description:
Goldenrod City is a location introduced in Generation II.

Goldenrod City is a city in the southwest of Johto. It is the largest city of the Johto region and the fifth of the Pokémon World at large, after Unova's Nimbasa City and Castelia City, Kalos' Lumiose City and Galar's Wyndon. Goldenrod City is based on Osaka, the largest city in the real-life Kansai region, which Johto is based on.

The player can take the north exit to Route 35, leading to the National Park and the Pokéathlon Dome. The south exit leads to Route 34 and through Ilex Forest to Azalea Town.

In , , and the remakes , the player is required to battle Whitney for the Plain Badge. Once the player has obtained the seventh Gym Badge, Team Rocket takes over the Radio Tower, and its broadcasts are directed to contact Giovanni. After the player saves the Radio Director, the broadcasts return to normal.

entities.short_description: Violet City is located in the central part of Johto. Trainers visit Violet City to claim the Zephyr Badge from Falkner, the Violet City Gym Leader who specializes in -type Pokémon.
entities.description:
Violet City is located in the central part of Johto. Trainers visit Violet City to claim the Zephyr Badge from Falkner, the Violet City Gym Leader who specializes in -type Pokémon.

The population of Violet City is 35, making it the second-largest city in the Johto region.

The largest structure in the city is the Sprout Tower, a wobbling pagoda that is being taken care of by Sages, who train Pokémon of their own. After the player defeats the last Sage, they will receive HM05 (Flash). Besides the Sages, Bellsprout and Rattata can be encountered inside the tower during the day, and Gastly can be found at night.

The majority of the sages use Bellsprout on their team, but one of the trainers in the very top floor uses a Hoothoot. In addition, the Elder, Li, does too.

entities.short_description: Diantha is a graceful woman whose elegance perfectly reflects her status as both Kalos' Champion and a celebrated movie actress. She has a slender figure, delicate features, light blue eyes enhanced by violet eyeshadow,…
entities.description:
Diantha is a graceful woman whose elegance perfectly reflects her status as both Kalos' Champion and a celebrated movie actress. She has a slender figure, delicate features, light blue eyes enhanced by violet eyeshadow, and short dark grey hair styled into a distinctive star-like shape with raised front bangs. Calm, composed, and effortlessly poised, she carries herself with quiet confidence and sophistication. Her beauty and fame attract constant attention throughout Kalos, prompting her to occasionally wear disguises so she can travel in public unnoticed.

Diantha's attire is elegant and fairy-like, consisting of a pristine white outfit accented with gold trim. She wears a long white blazer with broad lapels, decorative buttons, petal-shaped tails, and gold-lined cuffs over a simple white top with matching gold accents. Attached to the back are two lace-like, cloud-shaped ornaments resembling wings, enhancing her ethereal appearance. She completes the outfit with white shorts, a white choker, white low-heeled boots, and a soft pink handbag. Around her neck hangs a gold swan-shaped Mega Charm, which she uses to Mega Evolve her partner Pokémon, Gardevoir. Together, her attire blends elegance, fantasy-inspired beauty, and Champion-worthy sophistication.

Diantha is considered to be beautiful and famous by many people around Kalos that this causes her to gain too much attention due to her roles as both a successful movie actress and Pokémon Champion, hence why she wears disguises to move around in public without being recognized.

Diantha seems to be a polite and classy woman who talks formally, and she is kind to the player character when they challenge her once more. She views the bond between Trainer and Pokémon to be of the utmost importance for growth. Such focus allows her to communicate to Gardevoir how and when to dodge simply by making eye contact and looking in a certain direction, as showcased in Pokémon the Series.
