entities.name: Volo
entities.short_description: Volo is a character appearing in , who is the central antagonist.
entities.description:
Volo is a character appearing in , who is the central antagonist.

Despite seemingly being an unsuspecting merchant from the Ginkgo Guild, it is later revealed that he is a direct descendant of a group of prestigious ancient Hisuian people called the Celestica and also the main culprit who caused the rampage of Legendary Pokémon Dialga/Palkia, causing the sudden space-time rifts while attempting to summon Giratina and use it as a pawn in order to force Arceus out of hiding.

Volo is a tall and lean man with an energetic yet composed demeanor, standing with an easy confidence that suggests both charm and capability. His height and slender build give him a graceful, almost agile appearance, fitting for someone constantly on the move. He has a youthful face with sharp, refined features—his eyes are keen and expressive, often carrying a mix of curiosity and mischief, hinting at his inquisitive and ambitious nature. His blonde hair is long and flows smoothly, with several strands sweeping dramatically to one side, giving him a slightly wild yet deliberate look that complements his personality. The light color of his hair and fair complexion accentuate his striking, adventurous aura. When he smiles, it is both warm and mysterious—an expression that invites trust but conceals deeper intentions beneath its surface.

Volo's clothing, as shown on the right side of the image, is practical yet distinctive, suited for travel while still stylish and emblematic of his merchant persona. He wears a blue and orange outfit with fur-lined accents around the collar and cuffs, combining warmth and flair. Over his attire, he dons a white apron-like garment adorned with a golden emblem—a symbol of his merchant guild—which contrasts neatly with the darker blue beneath. His pants and boots are sturdy and travel-ready, designed for long journeys across rough terrain. A large, cylindrical backpack rests on his shoulders, striped in matching orange and white tones, suggesting his preparedness and his role as a traveling merchant. Completing his look is a matching blue-and-orange cap, worn casually over his long blond hair tied in a bun , giving him an approachable and roguish charm. Every element of Volo's outfit reflects his dual nature—part friendly wanderer, part enigmatic figure driven by hidden motives.

entities.name: Candice
entities.short_description: Candice serves as the Gym Leader at the Snowpoint City Gym. She specializes in -type Pokémon and holds the Icicle Badge for the trainers that can defeat her.
entities.description:
Candice serves as the Gym Leader at the Snowpoint City Gym. She specializes in -type Pokémon and holds the Icicle Badge for the trainers that can defeat her.

Candice has black hair tied into pigtails with blue scrunchies and amber eyes. She also has blue pins on both sides of her hair. She wears an elbow-length long sleeved white blouse, a blue bow on her chest, a short brown skirt that reaches her thighs, and a blue cardigan most of the time tied around her waist but sometimes when just talking worn on top of her white shirt. Candice also wears knee-length white and blue striped socks and brown shoes.

Candice is a very sociable trainer and a bit of an oddball to say the least, breaking the stereotype of ice-type trainers being cold and untouchable. Her choice of clothing given her type specialty, may suggest she enjoys the cold a little too much. Embracing her youthful appearance, Candice is cheerful, happy-go-lucky and warmhearted among her peers, and has a fervent passion on focusing on doing things she loves, such as Pokémon battling, trends and romance.

The name Candice comes from "ice", as she is an -type specialist.

entities.short_description: Cabo Poco is a location introduced in Generation IX.
entities.description:
Cabo Poco is a location introduced in Generation IX.

Cabo Poco is a small town located in the South Province of the Paldea region.

The player's house, called Your House in the game, is where the player and their Mom live just before joining the academy. It is a Flying Taxi spot, available since the start of the game.

Mom can heal up the player's Pokémon (and also charge up their Tera Orb in the process. Mom will also provide recipes for Veggie Sandwiches and Nouveau Veggie Sandwiches. Two Squawkabilly that can be battled and caught also appear on the roof.

entities.description:
The Los Platos Pokémon Center is situated in the southeastern corner of the town. The player can heal their Pokémon, buy and sell items, create TMs and exchange TM Materials for LP in these Pokémon Centers, and join with other players using the Union Circle.

During the player's first visit to the town, Nemona will teach the basics of a Pokémon Center's functions.

The Entrance Hall connects to the outdoors of Naranja/Uva Academy and the rest of Mesagoza. The player can attend or revisit a class by checking in at the front desk in front of the entrance door. The rest of the hall contains numerous books that the player character can read.

The Cafeteria provides different types of food that the player can buy to obtain Meal Powers. It is also where the player meets Cassiopeia for the first time.

entities.name: Iono
entities.short_description: Iono is a character from . She is Gym Leader at Levincia's Gym in the Paldea region and specializes in -type Pokémon. Iono is also is a streamer and influencer who has a livestream titled Iono Zone.
entities.description:
Iono is a character from . She is Gym Leader at Levincia's Gym in the Paldea region and specializes in -type Pokémon. Iono is also is a streamer and influencer who has a livestream titled Iono Zone.

Iono is a young girl of a slightly short stature. She wears a yellow sweater and a pair of Magnemite-shaped hair pins that seem to move on their own, mimicking her expressions. Under her sweater she is wearing a halter neck top exposing her shoulders. Iono also has light blue and pink hair with a bow shaped design in the front and sharp, pointed teeth. She also wears a necklace and a pair of metallic grey boots, each attached with a metal screw. A single grey legging covers Iono's right leg, while a single black strap is tied onto her left leg.

Iono is a perky, vivacious and over-the-top celebrity. She is also tomboyish and brash, referring to herself as "boku", while also being cutesy. She has a habit of "smashing languages" together while moving animatedly, which she calls "Iono-ese".

She is also highly enthusiastic with her fame and career, particularly caring for subscriptions by collaborating with popular figures. Through her conversations with her fellow Gym Leaders, more of her personality can be seen; she has an inferiority complex to Tulip, clashes with Brassius (who claims she doesn't know the meaning of "avant-garde"), while Grusha believes that she is more interested in maintaining numbers than the content of her streams. She also used to read comments, but stopped after an incident because of "THOSE fans", implying that she is not used to negativity.

entities.description:
Melony is a character that was introduced in Generation VIII. She is the Gym Leader at Circhester's Stadium and specializes in -type Pokémon. She can only be fought in Pokémon Shield—in Pokémon Sword, her son Gordie replaces her as Gym Leader (though he specializes in types instead of Ice types).

Melony is a large, plump woman with fair skin, gray-blue eyes, and lightly painted fingernails. She has voluminous light gray hair that falls to her hips, along with a grayish-blue streak and a single unruly bang. For clothing, she wears thick clothes suitable for cold weather. Her outfit consists of a white turtleneck sweater with the -type and Gym Challenge symbols on it, a puffy white scarf, and a large white wool hat. She also wears blue-gray tights with white patterns and white shorts with a black design, her Gym number, and the -type symbol on them. To complete her outfit, she wears long white boots and a white and black glove on her right hand.

True to her name, Melony is usually a sweet lady. In terms of her Gym, however, she seems rather calm and reserved. She trains in a strict way analogous to the Spartan method, and it's speculated that her battle style is influenced by a bicker she had with her son, Gordie. Compared to the refined and graceful battle style of her son, Melony loves a hard battle.

However, Melony doesn't seem to take losing well, as when she is defeated in battle, she talks about how she apparently wants to crawl in a hole.

entities.short_description: Katy is a character appearing in Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet. She is the Gym Leader at Cortondo's Gym and is one of the eight Gym Leaders in which the player can fight in any order they chose. She specializes in…
entities.description:
Katy is a character appearing in Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet. She is the Gym Leader at Cortondo's Gym and is one of the eight Gym Leaders in which the player can fight in any order they chose. She specializes in types.

Katy is a slightly plump woman with teal hair and brown eyes. She has a fair-skinned appearance. Befitting her secondary job as a pastry chef, she wears a chef uniform consisting of a light-gray blouse with a matching hat and gloves, a brown ascot, a matching long brown skirt and a waist apron of the same color of her skirt. She also has a spider web on her apron and wears brown tights and white shoes.

Her -type preference is reflected in the many antennas in her clothing and also her waist band giving the impression that she has a segmented body much like a real bug.

Katy is compassionate and kind-hearted. She enjoys the nature of -types and loves to cook. Despite her friendly personality, Katy takes Gym battles seriously, although due to her Gym being frequented by aspiring Trainers, she usually doesn't get the chance to go all out. This changes when after the rematch, Katy realizes that going easy on early trainers is not doing them any favors and decides that she is going to give them a stronger taste of reality, implying that while she is outwardly sweet and kind, her motherly personality inside wishes to instill some discipline in young trainers who are looking to better themselves, putting in the same level of effort she does for her pastry shop and doing things "the old-fashioned way".

entities.short_description: Clair has pale skin, blue eyes and light blue hair, tied in a high ponytail with a beige hair band. Two large spiked fringes frame her face and point outward, and a third fringe rests in the center of her face between…
entities.description:
Clair has pale skin, blue eyes and light blue hair, tied in a high ponytail with a beige hair band. Two large spiked fringes frame her face and point outward, and a third fringe rests in the center of her face between her eyes. She also has very thin eyebrows, and visible eyelashes.

Clair wears a high-neck dark blue suit that extends to her thighs, with two shoulder pads, which have two yellow circles and a black cape on her back which its interior is red. Clair also wears a pair of dark blue fingerless gloves and a pair of dark blue high heeled ankle boots.

She wears a black and maroon cape with beige shoulder pads, a two-tone blue and light blue skin-tight bodysuit, blue gloves with black bracelets on her wrists, and a pair of blue knee-length high heeled boots with black anklets. Clair also wears a blue gem on her neck, resembling a Dragonair's pearl, and beige earrings, shaped like a dragon's tooth.

Clair holds a great deal of pride in her appearance — much like Lance does. Her competitive and tough, prideful attitude is often seen as both inspirational and intimidating to some, though it can sometimes get the best of her, similarly to Silver.

The is one of the Paldean Gyms that have to be cleared for Victory Road. The Artazon Gym specializes in -type Pokémon, and the gym leader is Brassius.

For the gym test, the player must find 10 Sunflora across Artazon. It is moderately easy, and the player just has to check the maze for Sunflora.

Brassius may be easy at first, his Petilil and Smoliv aren't as hard as they look. Brassius's real problem is his Sudowoodo. It is is a type, which shatters and types. Luckily, it Terastallizes into a type, but still knows Rock Throw. If the player's types and types get knocked out, a can take care of Rock Throw. The player is awarded the Grass Badge when he is beaten.

entities.short_description: The Cortondo Gym is a location introduced in Generation IX.
entities.description:
The Cortondo Gym is a location introduced in Generation IX.

Cortondo Gym is a gymnasium located in the Paldea region, and the Gym Leader is Katy. This gym specializes in -type Pokémon. This gym is very close to Mesagoza, so many students at Naranja and Uva Academies go here to have their first Pokémon Battle at a gym.

The gym test requires the player to roll an olive to the finish line. You can ride on Koraidon to push it. There are also shortcuts, but to e able to use them, you have the battle the shortcut guard. The shortcut guard only has a Smoliv, so if you have a Fuecoco or Crocalor, it will be easier to battle the guards and the gym leader. Once you are finished with the Olive Roll, you may challenge Katy to a gym battle. By winning, the player can obtain the Bug Badge.

Katy owns a Nymble that can do Struggle Bug, so get a Houndour not only because it is part -type, but also because it outspeeds. Katy has a Tarountula that can use Assurance, but Hondour can be protected from this because it is part -type. Katy sends out her terastallized, Teddiursa, you may have a Tera Battle against Katy, as long as your Houndour terastallizes into a -type and not a -type, as is good against dark. If your Houndour is knocked out and you do not have a Fuecoco, bring in a -type like Staravia or Fletchling.

entities.description:
Geeta is a character appearing in , who is the chairwoman of both the Pokémon League in Paldea, for which she also serves as the region's Top Champion, and the region's academy.

Geeta has a regal and commanding presence, reflected in her tall, slender stature and poised demeanor. Her facial features are sharp and elegant—almond-shaped violet eyes framed by long lashes, arched brows, and a calm, confident expression. She has a warm, medium-dark complexion and wears subtle makeup that enhances her dignified appearance, including violet eyeshadow and defined eyeliner. Her long, flowing black hair, streaked with gray and gold, adds to her majestic look, and a distinct blue headpiece-like bang frames her forehead. Geeta's overall appearance is refined and authoritative, fitting her role as the top Champion and Chairwoman of the Paldea Pokémon League.

Geeta's clothing is formal, elegant, and symbolic of her high-ranking position. She wears a sleek, black double-breasted suit jacket adorned with glossy buttons, paired with matching tailored trousers that emphasize her tall, commanding figure. The jacket features bold gold vertical stripes descending from the collar, adding a regal touch, while the cuffs of her sleeves are decorated with intricate blue detailing—one side bearing a stylized sun symbol, perhaps signifying her authority or status. Her gloves are asymmetrical in design: the left is long and blue with the sun insignia, while the right is shorter and more fitted. A high-collared undershirt in deep blue and black, with a subtle star-like pattern, adds depth to the ensemble. Polished black dress shoes complete the outfit, reinforcing her dignified, professional image. Her attire exudes power, precision, and prestige, perfectly mirroring her role as the top Champion of the Paldea region.

Geeta's personality is composed, authoritative, and deeply professional, fitting her role as the Chairwoman of the Pokémon League and top Champion of the Paldea region. She carries herself with poise and confidence, often speaking in a formal and respectful manner that reflects both grace and control. Geeta is highly disciplined and holds high standards—not just for herself, but for others as well—believing in excellence, order, and responsibility. Though she may come across as distant or overly formal at times, her demeanor is not cold; rather, it reveals a deep sense of duty and commitment to maintaining the integrity of the League. She takes great pride in guiding the region's development and fostering rising talent, showing a visionary mindset. Calm under pressure and never boastful, Geeta embodies the quiet strength of a seasoned leader who values structure, tradition, and the growth of those under her guidance.

Paldea is a region that was introduced in Generation IX. It is where takes place and is seemingly based off the real-world . Its name was revealed on August 3, 2022.

A small town on a cape in the south of the Paldea region. It is the hometown of the player and their rival, Nemona.

A focal point of the region, the institute is said to have a history that exceeds other schools. The campus the player attends will depend on the version they play. They are run by the director Clavell.

A town that's famous for its flowers and art. It has a windmill, small houses, and fresh greenery everywhere. Appropriately enough, Brassius is the Gym Leader here. He specializes in Pokémon and is known as the 'Verdant Virtuoso'.

entities.description:
Carmine is a character appearing in . She is a student attending in Blueberry Academy.

Carmine is a slender young girl with yellow eyes and black hair with red highlights. Her accessory on her head is a yellow headband and her outfit is a buttoned blue shirt, a white belt, a yellow fanny pack, a red thumbless glove, blue pants with two stripes on the legs, one white and one blue and red and white shoes. She is seen with a beauty mole, very light lipstick, and her eyes being half-closed.

In The Teal Mask, Carmine is seen wearing her blue Traditional Jinbei outfit.

Carmine is described to have a strong will, but is sometimes a bit selfish. She deeply cares for her younger brother Kieran despite initially being a bit rough on him, though she is sometimes oblivious to his feelings, which further complicates matters. Whenever she gets angry, her eyes generally widen and she shakes her hands violently.

entities.short_description: is a character appearing in . He is the former president of Exceed, Gibeon's estranged son-in-law, and Amethio's father.
entities.description:
is a character appearing in . He is the former president of Exceed, Gibeon's estranged son-in-law, and Amethio's father.

It is also implied loves his late wife Maria deeply, still wearing his ring even years after he was widowed.

As implied by Gibeon, was formerly a member of the Explorers when he was inducted as a young man, before he quit due to ideological differences and became the president of Exceed. This decision had led to him being exiled by his own father-in-law, who was furious by his deviation. However, his boss is still Gibeon, who monitors his every decision for the company.

When Professor Friede, who is a former employee of Exceed, tried to gain information from Crave about the rumored Eternal Grace related to Terapagos, said he could not provide any concrete answers due to pressure from higher-ups. However, he still gave Friede the latter's staff ID for Friede to access certain areas of the company.

entities.description:
Kahili is a character appearing in Pokémon Sun and Pokémon Moon. She is an Elite Four member who specializes in types of the Alola region.

Kahili has light bluish-white hair in the shaped like Swanna's wings with a cowlick. Her eyes are light blue and has a beauty mark near her left eye. Kahili wears a sky blue visor with a tiny orange patch. Her polo is a light cornflower gray-blue with sky blue stripes, matching her hat, with two blue dot patterns on her polo. Kahili's black golf club has the orange and yellow-colored handle, resembling a Toucannon's beak. In addition, Kahili wears a Z-Ring on her left wrist, orange knee-high socks with a white strip at the top, and white golf shoes.

Kahili loves golf and is an expert in the sport. She also loves and uses Flying-type Pokémon. Kahili appears to be prim and having high standards, perhaps a surprising trait for someone so young in age.

Kahili undertook the Kahuna challenge a long time ago. She went to other regions to become a better Trainer and a golfer. Hearing the Pokémon League would be established, Kahili flew back to Alola and became the Elite Four member, per Kukui's proposal.

entities.description:
Molayne is a character appearing in Pokémon Sun and Pokémon Moon. He is a former Trial Captain and Sophocles's cousin. In Pokémon Ultra Sun and Pokémon Ultra Moon, he replaces Hala as a member of the Elite Four who specializes in types.

Molayne is a man with three-layered hair: the bottom one being dark-colored, the middle one brown, and the top being colored light-colored. His eyes are colored grey. He wears a blue jacket with red stripes around his fore-arms, a teal collared shirt with two stripes tied in a knot, some black pants and shoes. He also has hexagon-shaped glasses with a grey frame.

Molayne and his Japanese name, Maarein, both come from mullein, an alternative name to the plant genus known as verbascum. It could also include molybdenum, a metallic element.

Molayne is a former Trial Captain, who passed the role onto his cousin, Sophocles. Now, Molayne takes care of the Alola's Pokémon Storage System.

entities.description:
is a character appearing in . He is one of the members of the Blueberry Academy BB League's Elite Four, specializing in types.

Drayton is a young man with short spiky hair, with a long single hair tuft with a purple streak, as well as a pair of yellow eyes. He wears a white t-shirt that is covered by a black/gold tracksuit, which has the design of a gold Maschiff on the back and sleeves. He also wears a purple cape tied down around his waist.

Drayton is very laid back and relaxed, often living a "lazy" lifestyle; Carmine states that he had been repeating classes for three years. Despite his seemingly lazy exterior, he does care about his friends and is a proficient trainer; his fellow member Lacey, who has an advantage over him with -types, has not beaten him once.

Whenever something disappoints or embarrasses him, his long hair tuft and the smaller tufts droop down.

entities.short_description: Eri is the boss of Team Star's Fighting Crew, a student at the Naranja/Uva Academies, and a major antagonist in the Starfall Street storyline of Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet. She specializes in -type Pokémon.
entities.description:
Eri is the boss of Team Star's Fighting Crew, a student at the Naranja/Uva Academies, and a major antagonist in the Starfall Street storyline of Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet. She specializes in -type Pokémon.

Eri is a tall girl that themes herself after the lucha libre much like Hawlucha in her Team Star attire. She wears a completely white outfit with knee-high leg warmers and boots underneath. With her outfit, she wears knee and elbow padding, showing she's well prepared for a fight. Rather than a luchador mask, she wears face paint with similar styling using blue, pink and purple, with white "fangs" next to her mouth to add a sense of intimidation. A black star with a white lightning bolt is above her left eye. The colored used in her outfit are muted, wearing white eye contacts and a wig of wavy white hair, making it so that most attention at first is drawn to her face and intimidating expression.

In her academy uniform, Eri's face is revealed, appearing rather youthful and has black hair that falls down to her shoulders. She wears a white shirt with academy colors and the academy's insignia. She also wears shorts with a floral pattern, knee-high socks and academy-themed shoes.

Eri's -type preference is reflected in how she casually dresses as a Joshi pro wrestler. Wearing face paint and clothes that enhance the appearance of her hands and feet similar to Sneasler's appearance. Fighting type is known as being the "Justice type" to contrast Dark type being "Evil" and thus despite Eri being a boss of Team Star, she is fiercely protective of her friends. Coincidentally she is the tallest, reflecting a trend that Fighting types are bigger and taller and more "human" than other pokemon as the Fighting type regional variants indicate.

entities.name: Arven
entities.short_description: Arven is a character appearing in . He is an upperclassman at the Naranja Academy or Uva Academy and a researcher of healthy recipes. He is also Professor Sada's and Turo's son.
entities.description:
Arven is a character appearing in . He is an upperclassman at the Naranja Academy or Uva Academy and a researcher of healthy recipes. He is also Professor Sada's and Turo's son.

Arven has a relaxed yet slightly rugged appearance that hints at his outdoorsy nature and love for cooking. He wears a white school shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a blue tie, and dark blue pants, giving him a loosely formal look. Over his shirt, he sports a bright yellow sleeveless vest with utility pockets, featuring the academy emblem, adding a practical touch to his outfit. His sturdy hiking boots and thick yellow-laced shoes suggest he's often out exploring. Arven's wavy, ash-blond hair falls over one side of his face in a large swoop, partially covering one eye and adding a laid-back charm to his demeanor.

Arven can be seen as snappy and irritated when first met. However, as the player helps him gather the Herba Mystica, he starts to become more friendly and nicknames them "Little Buddy". While still snappy, he is considerably less so than the beginning of the game. He views Nemona negatively, calling her a "battle freak" and would rather go to someone else for help rather than her if possible.

Arven is also displayed to cherish those he loves and cares about, majorly evident when he went through great lengths by searching for the Herba Mystica just to cure his injured Mabosstiff. While he also cares for his parents, he was not on good terms with them as they spent their time researching more than playing with him. However, upon learning that his true parent had died, he was saddened and felt some kind of kinship with the robotic replacement.

entities.name: Lacey
entities.short_description: is a character appearing in . She is a second-year student attending Blueberry Academy and the second-strongest member of the BB League's Elite Four. She specializes in type Pokémon.
entities.description:
is a character appearing in . She is a second-year student attending Blueberry Academy and the second-strongest member of the BB League's Elite Four. She specializes in type Pokémon.

Lacey is a slender girl with fair skin, with slightly thick brows, and down turned bronze yellow eyes. Her hair is styled to be shoulder length with fringe that is evenly trimmed above her eyes. Her hair color is ash pink with lighter pink under lights, with her signature tear drop shaped gold hair clips with blue gems. Her clothes consists of the academy's autumn uniform: a white sailor collar shirt with the red neckerchief held with a blue clip, blue pants with one blue stripe and one white, with white sneakers, and red thumbless gloves. Over her uniform she wears a long lavender knit cardigan that nearly reaches her legs with three buttons, a ruffled knit design around the shoulders and bows that are meant to reference her fairy type speciality. Like her father, she is of at least partial Sinnohan descent, effectively making her the equivalent of a Japanese-American.

Reliable and skilled in Pokémon battling, Lacey adores cute Pokémon, particularly -types. She is known for her strict adherence to rules and traditions, her love for cute Pokémon, and her role as a reliable guide for new students. Her sense of responsibility and being by the book is possibly due to her father, Clay, being a lawyer and a Gym leader, and wanting to follow his example. Though her habit of crossing her arms in an "X" fashion to show her disapproval of something shows she does have a playful side.

Lacey's name ties with some words like "youthful" and the Araceae genus plant family that includes taro.

entities.name: Mela
entities.short_description: Mela is the boss of Team Star's Fire Crew, a student at the Naranja/Uva Academies, and a major antagonist in the Starfall Street storyline of Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet. She specializes in -type Pokémon.
entities.description:
Mela is the boss of Team Star's Fire Crew, a student at the Naranja/Uva Academies, and a major antagonist in the Starfall Street storyline of Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet. She specializes in -type Pokémon.

Mela is a young woman with short red hair with a strand of yellow hair sticking out, and the top is a pale-yellow color, the bottom looks like it sticks to her face while being fluffy, the top looks like a flower that's facing down, and 'horns' split into two in her hair, as well as freckles and green eyes. She wears a strapless black bodysuit with a white top showing the Naranja or Uva Academy emblem, black finger less gloves, a orange/purple collar and a loose belt, red boots with the Team Star emblem.

In her academy attire, Mela's hair is rearranged into a shoulder length bob cut, with the yellow strand rearranged towards the left side of her head. She wears a white shirt with the academy tie, with a gray jacket over it. She also wears academy shorts and shoes with black thigh-high socks.

Mela is described to be very steadfast and firm, always completing any task she has set on in order to maintain the loyalty of her teammates. She also is willing to solve any solution, although her methods of doing so is more heavy handed. Despite appearing tough and prone to anger, Mela is very kind and loyal to her friends. She is also surly, with Eri stating that it was to a way to make the bullies stop picking on her.

entities.name: Irida
entities.short_description: Irida is a character appearing in Pokémon Legends: Arceus. She is the leader of the Pearl Clan.
entities.description:
Irida is a character appearing in Pokémon Legends: Arceus. She is the leader of the Pearl Clan.

Irida's features and stature give her an air of youthful energy and quiet confidence. She has a slender, petite build, with delicate proportions that emphasize grace and agility rather than physical power. Her face is soft and expressive, marked by large, bright blue eyes that convey attentiveness and warmth. Her hair is a light blonde, cut in a short bob with longer strands framing the sides of her face, while the back is neatly layered. Her bangs part slightly to the side. Despite her youthful appearance, her expression often shows determination and a calm sense of leadership. Her overall posture is relaxed yet assured—someone who observes carefully and acts with purpose when needed.

Irida's clothing blends elegance with practicality, carrying a strong sense of cultural and symbolic design. She wears a sleeveless, form-fitting black tube top with a red stripe on top, paired with white shorts that allow for ease of movement. Around her waist is a teal kinchaku, adding a soft contrast of color. Draped over it is a distinctive large red-and-white Palkia-patterned obi. Her accessories include light blue bangles on her wrists and left ankle, which appear both ornamental and possibly functional, alongside an open-collar necklace adorned with a large pearl, and a crescent-shaped red headpiece. Completing her outfit are red-and-black obi shoes with thick white soles, combining comfort with a unique, ceremonial aesthetic. Altogether, Irida's outfit reflects her role as a spirited leader—balancing beauty, tradition, and readiness for adventure.

As the leader of the Pearl Clan, Irida admires the vastness of the Hisui wildernesses. At first, she seemed distrustful to the player and also harbored animosity toward Adaman, but gradually opens up to both of them. She is shown to be a grateful person, helping the player who has quelled Kleavor after they get temporarily banished by Kamado.

entities.description:
Indy is a character appearing in , who is a grunt working for Explorers, and as one of Spinel's henchmen.

Indy has sharp, angular facial features that give him a serious and somewhat aloof expression. His eyes are narrow and slightly slanted, with green irises that convey a focused and confident demeanor. His eyebrows are thin and sharply angled downward toward the center, adding to his stern look. He has a small, straight nose and a neutral, closed-mouth expression that doesn’t show much emotion. His hair is black with a slicked-back style, except for a few blue streaks and a distinctive blue strand that curves across his face.

He wears a sleek, light-blue suit with dark blue accents. The suit jacket has a dark blue collar, pocket trim, and shoulder sections, along with three dark blue buttons down the front. The sleeves have dark blue panels near the shoulders and a white circular emblem with a dark blue center on the upper arms. Underneath the jacket, he wears a dark gray dress shirt with a pointed collar, buttoned up neatly. His pants match the light-blue color of the jacket and are straight-cut, giving a formal and clean appearance. He also wears black gloves and dark shoes, completing his refined, uniform-like outfit.

entities.short_description: The Loyal Three is a trio of Legendary Pokémon that are mascots for the Generation IX games, .
entities.description:
The Loyal Three is a trio of Legendary Pokémon that are mascots for the Generation IX games, .

The Loyal Three consists of Okidogi, Munkidori, and Fezandipiti. According to Villager Folklore, the three nobly sacrificed themselves in order to drive out Ogerpon. However, according to the story passed down from The Maskmaker's bloodline, it is quite the opposite. The Loyal Three came to Kitakami due to hearing of the glittering masks of Ogerpon and the maskmaker. They stole them from the Dreaded Den and attacked the maskmaker while Ogerpon was away. In anger and defense, Ogerpon attacked the three, likely killing them. The villagers saw differently and made a monument in the Loyalty Plaza to remember them.

entities.short_description: Alain is a major supporting character appearing in Pokémon the Series and the Mega Evolution Specials. He is Ash's main rival in the Kalos region, and the eventual Kalos League Champion after defeating Ash in the…
entities.description:
Alain is a major supporting character appearing in Pokémon the Series and the Mega Evolution Specials. He is Ash's main rival in the Kalos region, and the eventual Kalos League Champion after defeating Ash in the finals. In Pokémon Journeys: The Series, he was revealed to have become one of the eight best Trainers in the world within the World Coronation Series, currently being ranked 6th.

Alain is a tall, slim teenager with messy black hair and blue eyes. He typically wears baggy gray pants, a black leather jacket, black boots, a blue shirt with a white undershirt, and fingerless gloves. He also has a pale blue scarf that resembles the flames emitted from Mega Charizard X's mouth. Alain also wore a Mega Ring on his left wrist, given to him by Lysandre, but at the end of the series, turned it over to the authorities as evidence proving the crime committed by Team Flare.

His retains the same outfit, his clothes are now more fitted compared to before. He also wears a new Mega Ring on his left wrist.

Alain is a calm, silent-type figure, who shows little emotion and focuses his attention towards battling. Deep down, however, he does not wish to see the ones closest to him suffer, especially his best friend, Mairin. Alain also obeyed Lysandre's orders without much hesitation, since Lysandre was the one that equipped him with the Mega Ring and the Charizardite X Mega Stone. In addition, Alain despises losing, with his loss to Siebold inspiring his desire to defeat 10 Mega Evolution trainers to become stronger.

entities.name: Ult
entities.short_description: His Japanese first-person pronoun is 「俺様 (oresama)」.
entities.description:
His Japanese first-person pronoun is 「俺様 (oresama)」.

Ult has a lively and mischievous expression, with large, bright brown eyes that give him a playful energy. His eyebrows are thin but expressive, often angled to match his spirited demeanor. He has a small, slightly pointed nose and a wide mouth that frequently curves into a confident grin or an excited shout, as seen in the different expressions on the concept sheet. His hair is a vivid green, shaggy, and unkempt, with long bangs that hang over his eyes and shorter layers in the back, adding to his adventurous look. The overall shape of his face is rounded but with a pointed chin, giving him a youthful yet determined appearance.

Ult's outfit is a mix of rugged practicality and casual style, perfectly suited for an adventurous traveler. He wears a short-sleeved black shirt with bright red rolled-up cuffs and matching red trim at the neckline, layered over a green undershirt that peeks out at the bottom for a pop of color. His dark gray, loose-fitting pants are cropped above the ankles and feature a frayed tear at the left knee, hinting at a life of active exploration and rough terrain. On his feet, he sports sturdy black slip-on shoes with red soles and trim, built for comfort and quick movement. A simple belt secures his pants, and a white wristband with a Mega Ring adorning his right wrist, adding a sporty touch. His most distinctive gear is a large, well-worn tan backpack with dark straps, carrying essentials for travel, including a bright yellow rolled-up sleeping mat fastened at the bottom—clear evidence that he's always ready for nights under the stars. Combined with his messy green hair and energetic demeanor, his clothing paints the picture of a spirited wanderer constantly on the move.

Ult is an abrasive, impulsive boy who often gets himself and Roy into trouble. He always acts as an attention-seeker who strives to be the strongest. He is secretly very lonely and craves for genuine friendships, but is unsure how to make friends properly. He also gets bashful easily at girls he doesn't feel familiar with.

entities.short_description: Tim Goodman is the main character from .
entities.description:
Tim Goodman is the main character from .

Tim has brown hair and black eyes. He wears a red sweater, blue pants, and blue with red sneakers.

Tim Goodman is a compassionate, caring, 18-year-old. He is a driven boy who is determined to help others when the opportunity presents itself.

Tim Goodman is the son of esteemed detective Harry Goodman, who has gone missing prior to the events of Detective Pikachu (video game). entities.name: Adaman
entities.short_description: Adaman is a character appearing in Pokémon Legends: Arceus. He is the leader of the Diamond Clan.
entities.description:
Adaman is a character appearing in Pokémon Legends: Arceus. He is the leader of the Diamond Clan.

Adaman possesses a striking and confident appearance, characterized by his tall, lean build and relaxed yet commanding posture. His features are sharp and youthful, with a defined jawline, slightly narrow eyes, and expressive brows that convey both determination and curiosity. His hair is a blend of deep indigo and greenish-gray, styled in loose, spiky layers that frame his face and flow backward, giving him a dynamic and energetic look. A small section of his hair is tied up in a short ponytail, adding a playful touch. His eyes are a vivid teal-green, exuding intensity and focus. Overall, his stature and features reflect both strength and poise—someone with confidence born from leadership and conviction.

Adaman's clothing is equally distinctive, blending traditional and modern design elements. He wears a long, open blue haori with rolled sleeves and yellow lightning-like patterns streaking across it, symbolizing his vibrant and decisive nature. The haori bears a bold emblem on the back, likely denoting his clan or group affiliation. Beneath, he sports a black tunic and loose, knee-length black shorts lined with yellow accents that complement the haori's design. His outfit includes black leggings and blue-and-black shoes adorned with tied details, offering a mix of practicality and flair. Accessories complete his look—silver rings, a blue gemstone pendant, a choker, and a single earring add an air of sophistication. The entire ensemble combines elegance, energy, and authority, perfectly mirroring Adaman's spirited personality.

Bold and forthright, Adaman holds the ideology of spending time to its fullest, and prefers hot-bloodedly bashing forward to do what he wants, leading to his initial conflict with Irida. However, he still is a reasonable person, like when he disagrees with Kamado unreasonably banishing the player. He is also a good leader who sometimes lectures some of his rather arrogant clan members like Melli, or tells Arezu to not rashly burden herself too much.

entities.short_description: Rystal is a recurring character appearing in . She is Lucius' wife, and Liko's great-great-grandmother.
entities.description:
Rystal is a recurring character appearing in . She is Lucius' wife, and Liko's great-great-grandmother.

As a young adventurer, Rystal had shorter dirty blonde hair tied into a bun, dark blue eyes, and her cheeks had two square shaped marks. She wore a green fedora with two long feathers in white and orange, white gloves, a green jacket and a pair of shorts with grey accents, a grey bodysuit, a carrier bag of blue and grey colors, black leggings, and a set of silver and grey boots.

As a mother, Rystal had longer hair that resembled a bobcut. Her ears were donned with a pair of orange, white and green patterened earrings. Her cheeks no longer had markings. She wore a dark green and maroon blouse, a long black skirt with maroon streaks, and dark brown shoes.

Like her husband Lucius, Rystal is a kind and adventurous person, and very compassionate to Pokémon in general. She had a deep bond with her Terapagos when she was alive. However, after being betrayed by Gibeon and losing her husband during her adventures in Laqua, Rystal decided to give up adventuring for the sake of her daugther Layla and in hopes of living a peaceful life.

entities.name: Perrin
entities.short_description: Perrin is a character appearing in . She is a traveler and photographer visiting Kitakami to take pictures of a certain Pokémon.
entities.description:
Perrin is a character appearing in . She is a traveler and photographer visiting Kitakami to take pictures of a certain Pokémon.

She is a descendant of Adaman, the leader of the Diamond Clan in Pokémon Legends: Arceus.

Perrin's features and stature convey a composed yet adventurous personality. She has a slender and athletic build, suggesting agility and confidence, with a posture that radiates focus and curiosity—traits fitting for someone constantly on the move and observing her surroundings. Her facial features are sharp and expressive, with defined cheekbones, narrow eyes, and a subtle, self-assured smile. Her eyes are a pale shade, giving her an alert and analytical gaze. Perrin's hairstyle is one of her most distinctive traits: her short, straight hair transitions from deep navy blue at the crown to a vivid, mint green at the tips, tied into a short ponytail at the back. A long section of hair falls over the right side of her face, softening her otherwise sleek appearance. She also wears medium-length nails that end in a square shape and are a barely noticeable white color due to her pale skin. Together, her stature and facial details project an image of calm competence mixed with a hint of playful independence.

Her clothing reflects practicality blended with a modern, edgy aesthetic. Perrin wears a cropped, sleeveless black top with wide shoulder straps, exposing her belly button and allowing freedom of movement. Over one shoulder, she carries a dark utility-style backpack secured by a strap across her chest. Her light-blue skinny jeans are high-waisted and feature black accents, including belt loops, seam detailing, and a side strap attachment for gear. She wears sturdy black-and-white hiking boots with thick soles, perfectly suited for outdoor exploration. A smartwatch adorns her left wrist, and she often carries a large professional camera with a leather strap—emphasizing her role as an observant documenter or photographer. The combination of her outfit's functionality and sleek design mirrors her adventurous, modern, and observant nature.

entities.name: Briar
entities.short_description: Briar is character appearing in . She is a teacher at Blueberry Academy.
entities.description:
Briar is character appearing in . She is a teacher at Blueberry Academy.

Briar is a woman with short wavy blonde hair with black iris, red-rimmed-and-white pupil eyes. She wears teal earrings resembling the Terastal phenomenon, a purple jacket, held by a black ribbed shirt, red pants and black loafers. The golden-colored designs on her shirt resemble that of the Scarlet/Violet book cover designs.

Briar is an ecstatic woman who spends a lot of her time researching the phenomenon of Terastalization in Pokémon. She, being the descendant of Heath, studies the Great Crater of Paldea and Area Zero in hopes of uncovering more of her distant ancestor. Her love for her research often causes her to lose focus on almost anything else and she often looses caution of how dangerous a situation can be because of it.

She holds the original Violet/Scarlet book written by Heath himself, which gives her access to information no-one other than her has.

entities.name: Rubina
entities.short_description: Rubina is a character appearing in , who is a grunt working for Explorers, and as one of Spinel's henchmen.
entities.description:
Rubina is a character appearing in , who is a grunt working for Explorers, and as one of Spinel's henchmen.

Rubina has sharp, confident facial features and a serious, determined expression. Her eyes are narrow with yellow irises, giving her a piercing gaze. Her eyebrows are thin, arched, and slightly angled downward toward the center, enhancing her assertive look. She has a straight, small nose and a neutral mouth set in a firm line, showing little emotion. Her hair is black with bold red streaks, styled with long bangs swept to the right side of her face and shorter strands framing her left side, while the rest is tucked neatly behind her head.

She wears a light-blue uniform with dark blue accents, similar in style to Indy's but with a few differences. Her jacket has dark blue lapels, pocket trim, and shoulder panels, along with a single dark blue button fastening it at the waist. On each upper sleeve is a white circular emblem with a dark blue center. Underneath, she wears a dark gray dress shirt, neatly buttoned. Her pants match the light-blue color of the jacket and are straight-cut, tucked into stylish dark shoes with slight heels. A prominent dark blue belt with a large gold oval buckle cinches her waist, giving her outfit a more fitted and authoritative appearance. She also wears black gloves, adding to her formal, commanding look.

entities.name: Paldea Elite Four
entities.short_description: The is a high-level Trainer Class and title given to four certain Pokémon Trainers that qualify as being the best Trainers in their respective regions, stronger than Gym Leaders and with only the Pokémon Champion above…
entities.description:
The is a high-level Trainer Class and title given to four certain Pokémon Trainers that qualify as being the best Trainers in their respective regions, stronger than Gym Leaders and with only the Pokémon Champion above their skill level, therefore serving as the penultimate of the games. There are currently 9 sets of Elite Four members and 1 Champion (3 in ), corresponding to the number of Generations that the main series games have been throughout the franchise (although Kanto and Johto share their respective Elite Four location, the Indigo Plateau, which, technically, is in the Kanto region).

In order to challenge the Elite Four, a Trainer must first acquire a total of 8 Gym Badges (16 in and , but can be fought at 8) upon defeating the Gym Leaders in a specific region. Upon battling these elite Trainers, the challenger must face all of them consecutively. Within the Pokémon League, they cannot access the Pokémon Center or Poké Mart without leaving the area until they successfully complete the challenge or losing at any point, making the battles against the Elite Four and soon after Champion an endurance match. In Generations I-IV, the members of the Elite Four are battled in a set order (including the remakes like in Generation VI, in Generation VIII) with gradually increasing levels per member. Since Generation V, they can be fought in any order, having a fixed level in their teams. They also employ strong healing items such as Full Heal or Max Potions (Full Restores in rematches). Once all four are defeated, the Trainer can now battle the regional Pokémon Champion for their title. However, in every region, if the player character is defeated at any point, including by the Champion, then they must re-battle all members of the Elite Four. In Generation IX, members of Paldea Elite Four are battled in set order, however members of BB League Elite Four can be fought in any order.

Apart from the official Elite Four, the Blueberry Academy also has their own unofficial version of the Elite Four in the form of the BB League. Rather than needing Gym Badges, a Trainer needs to complete a pre-trial in a manner similar to some Gym Leaders' before they can challenge them.

entities.short_description: Lucius is a recurring character appearing in . He is one of the main reasons Roy wanted to become a Pokémon trainer. He is also Liko's great-great-grandfather.
entities.description:
Lucius is a recurring character appearing in . He is one of the main reasons Roy wanted to become a Pokémon trainer. He is also Liko's great-great-grandfather.

Lucius is a young man who bears a close resemblance to Liko with a light complexion and light blue eyes. He has bright azure hair resembling Liko's haircut, tied back in a braid. He has a skinny build. He has a blue-and-gold striped cape, gold-accented brown boots, and black gloves with diamond appendages.

Lucius is a kind, brave man with a strong sense of determination. As the leader of his team, he cherishes his companions deeply and always treats others politely.

Lucius is derived from the Latin word for "light".

In Unova, after the player has obtained the eight Gym Badges of the Unova region, he or she will be able to travel to the Pokémon League (Unova) to take on four of the most powerful Trainers in the game, collectively known as the Elite Four. These Trainers are: {| style="text-align:center; color:#000; font-size:8pt" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"

In Pokémon Black and White, the first time the player defeats the Elite Four, there will be no Champion, as N has defeated Alder. This means he or she cannot enter the Hall of Fame, until the second time they battle them and finally defeat Alder to become the champion.

In Pokémon Black and White Versions 2, the Elite Four remain the same. Like in Pokémon Black and White, the player may battle the Elite Four in any order. After defeating the Elite Four, the player may challenge the new Champion, formerly Opelucid City's Gym Leader Iris, without interruption.

entities.name: Hala
entities.short_description: Hala is a character appearing in the games, Pokémon Sun and Pokémon Moon. He is the Island Kahuna of Melemele Island who specializes in types. He is also the grandfather of the player character's rival, Hau.
entities.description:
Hala is a character appearing in the games, Pokémon Sun and Pokémon Moon. He is the Island Kahuna of Melemele Island who specializes in types. He is also the grandfather of the player character's rival, Hau.

Hala is a stocky old man, who has white hair tied in a short spiky ponytail similar to his grandson Hau, as well as white eyebrows and moustache. He wears a blue shirt under a long sleeve yellow haori with some large flower pattern, a white rope tied in a knot over a red fan with black guards and white a pattern. He also wears knee length white shorts and blue flip-flops with white straps. In addition, Hala has squinty eyes, Hala also wears white wrist band on the left hand's wrist.

Hala is a caring grandfather to Hau. He prefers fighting types and respects the player character's power. Hala is a bold and seasoned trainer, though he's fatter than the typical trainer of his type specialty, Hala makes up for it with his go-getting perseverance.

Hala is the Kahuna of Melemele Island. In order to go to Akala Island, the player character must defeat Totem Gumshoos/Alolan Raticate and then battle Hala. Once the player character defeats Hala, Hala registers Tauros to the player character's ride pager.

entities.name: Johanna
entities.short_description: Johanna is a character first appearing in . She is the mother of Lucas/Dawn and lives in Twinleaf Town. Johanna has a larger role in the core series compared to Moms from previous generations.
entities.description:
Johanna is a character first appearing in . She is the mother of Lucas/Dawn and lives in Twinleaf Town. Johanna has a larger role in the core series compared to Moms from previous generations.

Since Johanna only appears as an overworld sprite game-wise, what she looks like can be hard to discern. From what can be gleaned from her sprite, Johanna has shiny blue hair cut into a bob, fair skin, and blue eyes. She wears a white long-sleeved shirt, blue pants, a pink apron, and red shoes. Overall, she greatly resembles her child.

Like every Mom that appears in the games, Johanna is kind, supportive, and always has the player character's back. She also instills good advice and values in her child, telling them to always treat their Pokémon with love and kindness. However, unlike most other Moms, Johanna is adventurous, easily bored, and not afraid to get out of the house. She regularly travels and can seen in different places throughout the player character's adventure, though she sometimes stays in Twinleaf Town and visits Barry's house while they're gone. There, Johanna talks to the rival's mom about her child, and vice versa.

In , at the start of the player's adventure, Johanna warns them not to go into the tall grass, because they do not have a Pokémon yet. She After the player character comes back home from an incident with some Wild Pokémon, Johanna gives them some Running Shoes and wishes them good luck on their journey. Later, when the player visits their Mom after going to Sandgem Town, she gives them the Guidebook (titled "Journal" in the original Generation IV games).

entities.name: Emma
entities.short_description: Emma is a character appearing in . Five years later, she's as a full on detective, taking over for Looker.
entities.description:
Emma is a character appearing in . Five years later, she's as a full on detective, taking over for Looker.

Emma possesses a noticeably softer, more vulnerable presence—one that hints at resilience still in the process of forming. Her facial expression is subdued and introspective, with slightly downturned brows and calm, observant eyes that suggest quiet thoughtfulness rather than overt confidence. Her features appear rounder and more youthful, lending her an earnest, almost fragile charm. Framed by voluminous, cloud-like dark hair that cascades in thick, unruly waves around her head and shoulders, her face often feels partially hidden, reinforcing a sense of emotional guardedness. Her posture is reserved and inward, shoulders relaxed but subtly drawn in, conveying uncertainty and restraint. She appears petite and slim, with a light build that emphasizes delicacy over strength at this stage in her life.

Her clothing reflects simplicity, wear, and practicality rather than intention or style. She wears a loose, long-sleeved blue top that hangs comfortably on her frame, visibly patched at the front—an unmistakable sign of modest means or prolonged use. Beneath it, a short orange-brown skirt adds a muted contrast, while opaque dark tights cover her legs, further emphasizing modesty and functionality. Flat shoes complete the outfit, unadorned and sensible. The overall ensemble feels lived-in rather than curated, suggesting she is focused on getting by than standing out. Altogether, her earlier appearance conveys quiet endurance and latent potential—a young woman still finding her footing, with confidence and self-assurance yet to fully emerge.

As Essentia, Emma's presence transforms into something sleek, controlled, and distinctly formidable—an embodiment of precision and technological authority. Her facial expression, visible only through the stylized visor of her helmet, is reduced to sharp, angular shapes that convey focus and emotional restraint rather than warmth. The faceplate's geometric design suggests a calculated intelligence, while subtle variations in the visor's configuration imply different operational states or expressions. Any trace of softness from her earlier self is deliberately concealed, replaced by an impassive, almost intimidating calm. Her posture is upright and balanced, poised with professional confidence, projecting readiness and discipline. Her stature appears taller and more imposing in this form, enhanced by the suit's structure and high-heeled boots, giving her a commanding, almost synthetic elegance.

entities.name: Cyrano
entities.short_description: Cyrano is a middle-aged man with dark skin, grey hair, green eyes, a mustache, and a soul patch. He wears a white fedora with a blue brim, a matching coat, both white shirt and trousers, a black and blue scarf, red tie…
entities.description:
Cyrano is a middle-aged man with dark skin, grey hair, green eyes, a mustache, and a soul patch. He wears a white fedora with a blue brim, a matching coat, both white shirt and trousers, a black and blue scarf, red tie and a black vest and matching shoes, with no socks underneath. He wears a silver wedding ring on his left ring finger.

Cyrano is said to be rather forgetful due to his age, often resulting in Briar and Lacey completing tasks in his place.

Cyrano is the founder and director of the Blueberry Academy in Unova. He befriended Clavell when they were young, and he was the one who suggested that he wear Premier Balls around his waist despite not using them.

After learning of the player through the joint field trip with Carmine and Kieran, Cyrano decides to invite the player to his academy as an exchange student.

The Lumiose Pokédex is introduced in Generation IX. The Pokédex starts with Chikorita and ends with Mewtwo, and mainly registers 232 Pokémon.

The Hyperspace Pokédex, which is a secondary feature with the Lumiose Pokédex, starts with Mankey and ends with Zeraora, and contains 132 Pokémon.

entities.name: Wy-Yes
entities.short_description: Wy-Yes, full name Wyatt B. Yessler, is a character appearing in , who was a member of the Rising Volt Tacklers.
entities.description:
Wy-Yes, full name Wyatt B. Yessler, is a character appearing in , who was a member of the Rising Volt Tacklers.

Wy-Yes is an adult man with short green hair and dark purple eyes. He normally wears a light teal green shirt with chest pockets, a brown belt with a yellow buckle, a yellow watch, and light grey trousers. As a journalist, he carries equipment such as notepads, a camera, a sunhat, and black bags.

Wy-Yes is a mischievous person who loves to exaggerate and prank others, or mix facts with rumors. Due to his constant lying, he and Mollie have a complicated relationship. However, he also believes that the truth depends on a person, and is ambitious about his own career as a journalist.

Wy-Yes was a member who joined the Rising Volt Tacklers two days before Mollie. At first, Mollie respected him, but she gradually stopped bothering to care about him after she got pranked by his equivocations and pranks more than once. Wy-Yes would later leave the Rising Volt Tacklers sometime before Dot joined, proclaiming that he wanted to become an authentic reporter, and had since been publishing articles and photographing Pokémon that also include Legendary Pokémon as part of his journalistic career.

entities.name: Master Mayonnaise
entities.short_description: Master Mayonnaise is a visually commanding character with sharp, angular facial features that reflect both age and confidence. He has a thin, well-groomed mustache and a pointed goatee, complemented by narrow eyes and a…
entities.description:
Master Mayonnaise is a visually commanding character with sharp, angular facial features that reflect both age and confidence. He has a thin, well-groomed mustache and a pointed goatee, complemented by narrow eyes and a smirking expression that suggest arrogance or self-assuredness. Subtle wrinkles around his eyes and forehead imply experience, adding to his intimidating presence.

He has a broad, muscular build and stands with a strong, confident posture—one hand resting on his hip in a stance that radiates dominance. His proportions, especially his wide shoulders and solid legs, reinforce the image of a powerful, seasoned warrior who is used to being in control.

His outfit is a unique blend of medieval armor and eccentric design. He wears large, shiny metallic shoulder pads adorned with piano key patterns—an unexpected and whimsical touch. His chest armor is smooth and polished, and a bright red, pleated skirt-like garment flows from his waist, contrasting with the metallic elements and adding dramatic flair. His arms and legs are armored as well, with gauntlets and greaves that suggest both mobility and defense, while his boots are large and sturdy.

Floating behind him are multiple turquoise discs with red centers, appearing to hover in formation. These add a mystical or technological aspect to his appearance, enhancing his visual impact and suggesting abilities beyond mere physical strength. Together, these elements create a character who is equal parts warrior, showman, and enigma.

entities.name: Litten Smitten
entities.short_description: Litten Smitten is a teenage girl with short black hair and bright yellow eyes. She wears an overall hooded jacket that resembles Nidothing, donned with different badges and logos, a black skirt, black socks with purple…
entities.description:
Litten Smitten is a teenage girl with short black hair and bright yellow eyes. She wears an overall hooded jacket that resembles Nidothing, donned with different badges and logos, a black skirt, black socks with purple diamond logos, and a pair of black sneakers with red accents. She also carries a purple-and-black backpack.

During one of Nidothing's live-streams, Litten Smitten accidentally lied about seeing the black Rayquaza after seeing that Nidothing's stream lacked comments. When meeting Liko and Roy, Litten Smitten was initially enthusiastic to meet fellow Nidothing fans, though she said that if she couldn't meet Nidothing, she wouldn't be revealing anything. But she soon became hostile when she learned that they were associated with the Rising Volt Tacklers.

Litten Smitten then challenged Liko and her Meowscarada to a battle, because she herself said she wouldn't trust anyone who had destroyed Mount Pericap. During the battle, Litten Smitten's Incineroar had the type advantage, but was outsmarted by Meowscarada, who had latched some of her Flower Trick's bombs onto its belt. However, after watching Captain Pikachu, Liko, and Roy calm down some enraged Fearow and Dodrio that were chasing Ult, Litten Smitten realized they weren't bad people and decided to trust them. She also admitted that her comment was just a lie and that it was meant to draw Liko out so she could meet her in person, since she was aware of how Liko used to be a regular commenter on Nidothing's streams. After receiving some encouragement from Nidothing and befriending Liko and Roy, Litten Smitten said she would support the Rising Volt Tacklers before she parted ways with them.

She later appeared in Levincia during the Nidothing and Iono Collaboration to participate in the handshake event.

entities.short_description: Dash is a character appearing in . She is the doppelgänger of Dot and therefore resembles her.
entities.description:
Dash is a character appearing in . She is the doppelgänger of Dot and therefore resembles her.

Her Japanese name, ボッコ Bokko, comes from a pattern-based respelling of ドット Dotto, officially romanized "Dot".

Her English dub name, Dash, comes from the word "dash". It starts with the same letter as Dot, and forms a possible reference to Morse code when combined (dots and dashes).

In Latin American Spanish, she is called Doki, a reference to [https://doki.fandom.com/es/wiki/Doki Doki], a character from the Latin American TV channel [https://discovery-kids.fandom.com/es/wiki/Discovery_Kids_(Latinoam%C3%A9rica) Discovery Kids], who appeared as the mascot from [https://youtu.be/ApFndzbnk_w?si=ciugoNZzXeKodzTi 2005] to [https://youtu.be/bylu43XYnHQ?si=MWjqLh6s7lcWLKJi 2019] and had his own animated series in [https://youtu.be/_mJbLx4lvsI?si=ORCk6KB7FJu3isMs 2013].

entities.name: Klara
entities.short_description: Klara is a rival appearing in Sword - The Isle of Armor Expansion Pass. She only appears in Pokémon Sword, and her Pokémon Shield counterpart is Avery. She specializes in types.
entities.description:
Klara is a rival appearing in Sword - The Isle of Armor Expansion Pass. She only appears in Pokémon Sword, and her Pokémon Shield counterpart is Avery. She specializes in types.

Klara is a slender young woman with fair skin, blue eyes, and pink hair. She also wears pink lipstick and eye shadow and has a mole under her mouth. She wears a wild, unique outfit with many accessories, including a white fur coat, a white and blue moth-like bow with pink circles on it, and a dark purple and green uniform. Her uniform consists of a multicolored collared shirt and dark blue shorts with the number 881 on them. Both her shirt and shorts also have quite a few designs and unique prints on them. For accessories, Klara wears a white bracelet on her left wrist, a Dynamax band on her right wrist, a thumbless purple and black glove on her right hand, and a white ring on her left hand. On her feet, she wears pink and white shoes with blue heels and knee-length stockings that have the same colors as her clothes.

Klara adores popularity and will put on a cutesy act just to win bystanders' attention. However, beneath her smiling face is a calculating mind that she will put to good use. Klara will not be afraid to use any underhanded tactics to ensure a victory, as seen during her last battle where she sabotaged the battlefield by deploying Toxic Spikes. This led to her downfall where Mustard, who already knew about Klara's cheating, sentenced Klara to care for the Dojo's Pokémon for six months.

Klara was a pop singer before becoming a Pokémon Trainer, though she was unsuccessful in promoting herself beyond selling eight copies of her first album. To become more popular, she decided she would try to become a Gym Leader, however she gave up after attempting for two days. She soon discovered the Master Dojo from a television program, and decided to try it out, thinking she wouldn't have to put in much effort in order to get stronger there.

entities.short_description: Kieran is a character first appearing in . He is a Pokémon Trainer, the younger brother of Carmine and a student attending Blueberry Academy.
entities.description:
Kieran is a character first appearing in . He is a Pokémon Trainer, the younger brother of Carmine and a student attending Blueberry Academy.

In The Teal Mask, Kieran is seen wearing a Traditional White Jinbei outfit. Instead of wearing a mask of the Loyal Three, he wears the Ogre mask.

In The Indigo Disk, Kieran wears a red sleeveless shirt and a white coat and is seen with the bangs of his hair pulled back except for a single strand. He claims that by pulling his hair back, he would be able to perform better in Pokémon battles.

Kieran is a quiet boy with a gentle nature who often hides behind his older sister, Carmine. He looks up to the player character, admiring them as someone cool and strong, and despite his timid demeanor, he harbors a deep desire to grow stronger. Unlike most people, Kieran sympathizes with Ogerpon and prefers her over the Loyal Three, recognizing her strength despite being alone. As the story progresses, he becomes increasingly jealous of the player for forming a bond with Ogerpon and ultimately capturing her. Notably, the French version of the game confirms that Kieran is 14 years old, while the Spanish version adds that he is going through puberty—something Carmine suspects is behind his shifting emotions and behavior.

entities.description:
Franka is a woman with dark indigo hair and dull purple tints, tanned skin, and purple eyes. She wears a pink neck scarf, a red jacket with a white collar and ruffles, a black top, a pair of dull brown baggy shorts, and a pair of brown slippers that resemble Rockruff.

Unlike her daughter, Dot, Franka is a talkative chatterbox. However, she also gets emotional easily, especially when it comes to expressing her affection for Dot.

Under Professor Friede's lead, Franka got onto the Brave Olivine to inform Dot that she would be taking Dot home. After Dot refused, and seeing Dot's Quaxly, Franka realized that Dot had become a Pokémon Trainer. She then challenged Dot to a battle, to which she lost after Quaxly defeated her Lycanroc. Franka then agreed to allow Dot to continue staying with the Rising Volt Tacklers after witnessing how much Dot had grown during her journey.

entities.description:
Brassius is a character appearing in Pokémon Scarlet and Pokémon Violet. He is the Gym Leader at Artazon's Gym, specializing in types and is one of the eight Gym Leaders in which the player can fight in any order they choose.

Brassius is a man with green hair resembling thorny vines and gray eyes with bags under them. He wears a red long-sleeved shirt with a yellow collar, black pants and green shoes. On his waist is a gray vine whip.

His Grass type preference is reflected in his thorny hair resembling spiny vines and his shirt having a thorny rose bud motif. His gray vine whip is often held like a portable garden hose, but likely has a dark thorny appearance to reflect his theme of "Every rose has its thorns" taken to the literal extreme.

Brassius is a stoic artist constantly looking for inspiration to reflect his love for conveying emotion. Though he appears extremely cold and scary, he tries to be kind and welcoming, but his scary appearance reflects his personal depression when he lost his way in life and was only able to find happiness again after Hassel showed him how to express himself with his art. He picked Sunflora as his model due to its perpetual grin no matter how upset its feeling. When it comes to meeting Trainers as a Gym Leader, he uses his depression as a vessel to energize his Pokémon battles and appear stronger as a Gym Leader, but he seems to care little about his role as a Gym Leader after having finally met a Trainer who can give him the inspiration he's been looking for.

entities.description:
Raifort is a character appearing in , who is the History teacher at Naranja or Uva Academy.

Raifort is a dark-skinned woman with purple hair tied in a ponytail and grey eyes. She wears a blue-collared shirt, golden semi-rimless glasses, blue jeans held by a brown belt, and shoes of the same color. For accessories, she wears a necklace resembling Articuno, a belt buckle resembling Lunala, a hair pin with Marshadow's face and a bracelet resembling the shell of Tapu Koko.

As her occupation suggests, Raifort is extremely interested in the ancient history of Paldea and thus prefers learning more about the past rather than new trends. Despite her obsession, she does have some restraint as she was forced to halt her hunt for the Ruinous Quartet after Clavell began suspecting her. Although knowing of the dangers of the quartet, she expressed a desire to let them out of their shrines for the purpose of studying them.

Coral is an admin of the Explorers and a major antagonist appearing in .

Coral is a short girl with rose-pink hair with medium-length bangs, which have two long strands hanging on the sides. Her hair is tied in two pigtails, fastened with white hairbands, and she wears a bandage on her hair.

Her eyes are dark brown, and she normally wears a black, baggy, shoulderless top with small pink spikes on the sides. Under her sleeves, she wears long pink nails, similar to the pink of her hair.

She wears a short, black skirt with a yellow pattern down the side, fastened by a yellow belt. Coral also wears a pair of high-top socks with a yellow patch on the tops. On her left leg, a patch is left empty, while on her right, she has a bandage just below her knee. Her shoes are black high-tops with a white band on the top.

entities.description:
Ryme is a character appearing in , who is the Gym Leader at Montenevera's Gym, specializing in -types.

Ryme is a dark-skinned middle-aged woman with white hair with braids; the front is braided into a skeletal hand, while the back is braided into a ribbon. She has wrinkles, green eyes; her eyelids and the bottom part of her lips are painted gold. She wears a black jacket with gold trim on the outside and completely gold on the inside. She wears a golden necklace, golden Poké Ball-themed earrings and a black baseball cap worn the opposite way with a gold closure on it. She also carries a microphone that has gold trim on it.

Ryme is a rapper who enjoys getting the audience fired up with both battles and rapping. However, she is also quick to anger, wanting to prove the power of Ghost Pokémon to Geeta and having no one to compete against in a rapping battle.

Ryme's name appears to be based on the word "rhyme", as she is a rap artist and rhyming is commonly used in songs and rap battles. It may also be a reference to rime, which is frost formed on cold objects by rapid freezing of water, because her gym is in a snowy enviroment.

entities.short_description: Spinel is the overarching main antagonist of . He is a former scientist who worked for Exceed, who secretly worked with the Explorers as one of the organization's admins. He later replaced Gibeon as leader of the…
entities.description:
Spinel is the overarching main antagonist of . He is a former scientist who worked for Exceed, who secretly worked with the Explorers as one of the organization's admins. He later replaced Gibeon as leader of the Explorers in a desperate gambit to get rid of Amethio, as well as becoming the now-former president of Exceed.

Spinel has teal hair with fluffy strands that extend down to his shoulders, with a dark teal tint near the end of his bangs. His eyes are narrow and two-toned, between soft pink and sky blue. His outfit is of a dark blue side-cape with a silver-and-blue gem clip, a black bodysuit, and a light teal coat and boots with yellow buttons and black accents.

During the one-year timeskip, Spinel has shortened his hair and adorned it with a blue gem, forming a ponytail. His coat and cape have become more partially dark blue, with their accents becoming more light yellow. He also wears an additional blue necktie.

As a child, Spinel had shorter hair, and wore glasses. His attire consisted of a pale blue long-sleeved shirt, a black belt, grey trousers, and dark brown shoes.

Onia, or Conia, is a former grunt of the Explorers who is also one of Amethio's subordinates and a former antagonist appearing in .

Onia has gray blue hair and eyebrows, and blue eyes. Her usual Explorers outfit consists of a grayish suit with an Explorers symbol on the left side of her outer shirt. She wears black skirts with light gray legwear and gray high heels.

When in her casual clothes during PH103, she wore a pale yellow shirt, a golden jumper, and a red bag.

Despite being part of the Explorers, Onia has been shown to be warmhearted, taking good care of Liko's Sprigatito when it was captured by Amethio. She was quick to give Sprigatito whatever it wanted such as food and toys. Onia tends to hide this side of herself, where she was quickly embarrassed after Amethio saw her playing with Sprigatito. Even when confronting it on the island, Onia didn't wish to have to fight the Grass Cat Pokémon and wanted it for herself.

entities.name: Alex
entities.short_description: Alex is a character appearing in Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire.
entities.description:
Alex is a character appearing in Pokémon the Series: Ruby and Sapphire.

Alex came to a mansion with his grandfather to play with the Shroomish, who lived in the neighboring forests. With the expansion of the town, however, the Shroomish vanished and Alex left the place, only to return later on.

Once the heroes met up at the mansion, Alex came to warn them the mansion was being demolished and it was dangerous to be there. The heroes told them they saw a Shroomish coming in. However, Alex denied that, since Shroomish vanished a long time ago, though he did hear about some spooky things in the mansion. The group entered the mansion and Alex actually saw a Shroomish. Team Rocket arrived to capture Pikachu, but everything was interrupted when hordes of Shroomish came. Team Rocket attacked the Shroomish, who emitted Stun Spore, causing Alex and the rest to leave the mansion. Alex saw the Shroomish were glad to see Alex and wanted to play again, so the heroes tried to convince Alex to stop the mansion from being destroyed. Team Rocket arrived once more, but were defeated by Shroomish and Pikachu. In the end, Alex decided to destroy the mansion, then to grow some new trees, to change the place into a forest for the Shroomish and promised to visit them more often.
